As she’d come to realize, she had never once been to this part of the campus on purpose. She’d been to the stadium in September, in a jersey that wasn’t hers with two stars drawn on her cheeks, spending most of the afternoon being stared at like a museum artifact. She could still smell the scent of sweat and grass in the air as she leaned against one of the bleacher poles, as she walked past, looking up at a boy she only knew as Mark’s smooth talker best friend, who looked at her with a glint in his eyes and muttered, this looks better on you.

This was very different from that evening in September.

This was four hundred yards past all of that, a low brick complex behind a fence with a lot in front of it. It was ten past five, already nearly fully dark outside, and the entire field was lit up in blinding lights.

She could hear it before she could see it, whistles, a repeated flat percussion of bodies and pads, somebody’s voice going hoarse over the top of it, followed by a horn. It went on for eleven minutes after she got there, before it’d stop the way weather did.

And Solar stood at the gate Chenle told her about with her hands in her coat pockets, watching a football program come apart into individual, somewhat normal people. Men in cut-off practice gear steaming faintly in the cold, someone laughing at something else, a cluster of them peeling toward a door she couldn’t see the other side of.

She had a whole thing prepared, one she had rehearsed on the walk over, which was quite a distance. It was casual, reasonable, beginning with something like hey I know you’re busy, but.

That was, until she saw her brother come out the back of the building.

Jeez.

She’d seen Jaehyun exhausted maybe a few times in her lifetime, never once by accident.

He had a tablet under one arm, his helmet hooked by the facemask in the other hand, talking to a man in a staff polo who was talking faster than he was, nodding at intervals, water bottle wedged under his other arm. His hair was wet and pushed flat off his forehead, a red weather across his cheekbones from the pads. As they walked, he rolled his right shoulder, slowly, two times in the unconscious way a person checks something they aren’t planning to mention.

The staff man had looked at him and said something that looked serious, and Jaehyun had pursed his lips and uttered, “tomorrow,” before the man had turned around and left.

His eyes seemed to realize something was in his vicinity, causing them to snap up, only to see his little sister standing there at the fence.

Yet, he didn’t look surprised. Jaehyun Lee probably hadn’t been since 2011. He made his way the several feet until he was standing before her, “Solar.”

“Hey,” she bluntly hums, “football thing seems too serious.”

Up close, he smelled like cold air, turf, and something medical. Oddly enough, he looked a lot bigger in this context than he was in any other, and she had the shocking thought that this was probably what everybody else on this campus saw when they said her brother’s name. “It is,” he confirms matter of factly. His eyes scanned her a single time, “are you cold?”

Though, it wasn’t said much like a question. “No,” she immediately responds, too quick for comfort.

“You’re not wearing enough layers,” he observed anyway, with a shake of his head, “it’s winter, Solar.”

“Is not,” she argues sassily, “I’m fine, Jae.”

“Uhuh,” he notes, setting his helmet down, which was, she understood, the closest thing she would get to go ahead, I have four minutes.

Neither of them said anything about the last time they’d spoken. That had been the phone call, three weeks ago, half past nine at night, and it resulted with her hanging up on him mid-sentence, and in the twenty two days since, he’d sent her exactly one thing and it had been before her tournament, wishing her luck. And she hadn’t ever answered that either, even if it did make her smile for a very split second.

So, the two siblings stood there in the cold, in the wash of a floodlight someone hadn’t switched off yet, two people who had grown up in the same room.

“The email,” she finally breathes.

Something in his face resolved, business, they were both much better at talking about business. “Yes.”

“I’m on it, you’re on it, from some lady I’ve never met, by the way, on behalf of mother,” she snorted, “which is the part I honestly cannot get over, most parents would send a text.”

“Mm, it’s Ms. Han, she’s new, you know,” he shares, leaning against the wall of the brick building.

“It opened with a table.”

“It’s a schedule, Solar.”

“It’s a table!”

“Schedule,” he corrects again, firmly, entirely unmoved, and Solar’s chest unclenched half an inch. The two of them being annoyed about the same thing from opposite directions was indeed the closest thing they had to a native language, it almost made her feel like she was still at home and not four hundred miles away up North.

And then, he went through the schedule in the order he did everything, the order it would happen in; arrival windows, the car, the foundation function that was a dinner which meant it had press assigned to it in limited capacity, a phrase he said without a flicker of irony since they’d both been hearing such words their entire lives.

“Do I have to go the Monday thing?” Solar whined, resisting the urge to stomp her foot on the grass like a child.

“Yes, Solar, you do have to go to the Foundation Dinner.”

“Okay, but is that like a for sure yes—”

“—Father will be there,” he cuts her off, and she huffed in defeat, since that was the whole answer in a nutshell.

Her eyes look out at the field, where two men were dragging something across the turf under the lights. “So, you’ll be there too?”

“Monday, yes,” he nods, “not Saturday or Sunday, we’re at Notre Dame Saturday, I come back with the team, and there’s a film treatment Sunday I cannot move.”

She blew air into her cheeks before puffing it out with a loud sigh, “so I’m alone.”

“That is what that entails.”

Two days, she calculated, two days on the Upper East Side with no one other than her parents and one of their grueling schedules. “Great,” she deadpans.

“It’s two days,” he affirms, “I think you’ll survive.”

“Yeah, I said great, didn’t I?”

Jaehyun stared at her for a second longer than the sentence deserved, but didn’t say anything else for a moment, which was either restraint or disinterest. She couldn’t tell which one.

“You need to confirm your travel before the fourteenth,” he informs instead, “I’d do it this week.”

“I know, it says it four times.”

“Then confirm it by the fourteenth,” he states again.

The wind blew through them in a rush. “Jae,” she grumbled out.

“I’m not being difficult,” he lectures, “if it isn’t confirmed, Ms. Han will call the house, and if she calls the house, you will then have to have a different conversation with mother than the one you want to,” he shifts the tablet under his arm, “so, I suggest doing it sooner than later.”

“Alright,” she snaps, “I’ve got it, President.”

He was looking at her with the complete face of someone who was unimpressed and very unamused, a look she knew very well. “I needed to talk to you, anyway,” he’d mentioned, just as she was about to decide she’d had enough for today.

And Solar felt her whole body change temperature, realizing she should’ve known, she should’ve known walking past the library, the dining hall, the long dark stretch of nothing before the athletic complex, that there was always something else, and she could only imagine who it was going to relate to. “Oh boy,” she exhales, her hands hitting her sides, “go on, go ahead.”

He didn’t react to her dramatic gestures in the slightest, “someone sent me something.”

“Even better,” she throws her hands in the air again, exasperated, “sent you what?”

“A photograph,” he hums, “from Halloween, I presume, you and Mark Lee,” he states, the way he said everything, a man reading a line item, “you know I don’t waste my time with those ridiculous accounts, but someone apparently believed I should know — for good reason.”

“For good reason?” she cries, “Oh, so it’s good that these accounts are stalking me?”

She could’ve said it then, Danielle Marsh, I know that’s who it was. She also told me shows I didn’t sleep at Alpha that night, but if I say her name out loud to you she’ll plaster it all over the internet for everyone to see.

“No one said that,” he corrects, “but I’m disappointed, to say the least.”

“Right, so you’re going to call father now?”

“No,” he deadpans, “I spoke to Mark.”

The floodlight buzzed above them, her stomach dropped into the face of the Earth. Her hands clench at her sides as she lets out a deep breathe to calm herself. “You — talked to Mark, again… when would you have done that?”

“Before practice.”

“Before practice,” she confirms.

“So, you got a picture of me, and you went and asked him,” she returns, slowly, like it was an equation.

“Well, yes, Solar, he is part of the problem here,” he retorts bluntly, “it is clear that you will not listen, although, clearly he will not either.”

So, they seemed to be at a crossroad, and she hated that it felt familiar. “What’d he say?” she asks instead. She had to know, because there was a version of her Friday night in her brother’s possession, likely multiple versions, ands he hadn’t been the one to put either of them there. She needed to know which version Mark’s was, not necessarily Danielle’s, there was no way to ask that didn’t feel like putting her wrists out.

“He said it was misleading,” he admits, hesitantly, “that he cares about you, you’re genuinely his friend, some kind of apology about how he can’t help but want to be around you.”

Her eyes nervously stared down at the turf, trying to imagine Mark Lee saying all of those things. Weirdly enough, it didn’t take much imagining. Mark had stood in front of her brother and reported what he knew of her evening with honesty, and whether he knew or not, not a single part of it included Haechan in his recollection.

“Okay,” she mutters.

“My concern is not that you’re friends with him,” he continues, “I’m concerned about how much of your time that house has, you are a freshman, you have a name attached to everything you do, and the two of them are the absolute worst choices—”

He cut himself off.

The two of them are the absolute worst choices, repeated in her head with an echoing screech. The sentence with the door in it, and her mouth was already opening with something in it that she had absolutely no business knowing.

I know what you said to him, his record, the third conversation, all of it, she wanted to say, I know there’s something more going on, I know that you know, otherwise you wouldn’t be so insistent about this.

It’s not only about my name.

She didn’t say any of it.

“—the two of them what?” she pends.

“We don’t need to pretend that you don’t already know.”

Somewhere behind him, a door opened and a voice called something with his name in it, two syllables and a question mark. He raised a hand to signal to them one moment without turning around.

“I’ve got treatment,” he informs before she could form the right words.

“Fine,” she breathes.

He locked eyes with her one last time, picking up the helmet. And then, unhurried, entirely calibrated, the way he’d typed good luck today sister into her phone three weeks ago and never mentioned it again. “It’s cold, you need to get back.”

“Jae, wait—”

“—Confirm the travel, Solar.”

He turned around and went back through the gate.

And Solar stood there, in the dark outside a building she wasn’t allowed into with a whole speech in her chest and nowhere to put it. Thank you for not telling him about the team, please don’t tell him about the two boys, either. In reality, she didn’t think he would, because if he really wanted to, he’d have done it by now, instead of going back and forth begging each of them.

There’s something more, she thought as she spun on her heel to begin the walk back, he knows it.

62: next time

At one forty in the morning, Solar Lee was lying flat on her back in the dark of her pink bedroom, fully dressed, with her shoes on. She'd been lying like that for twenty minutes.

Not a decision, she informs the ceiling, just thinking about the possibility of such a decision.

Naturally, she ceiling declined to comment.

The truth, which she was refusing to look at directly the way a person tries to avoid looking at a bill, was that she'd put her jeans on at midnight. In fact, the jeans were on before she'd begun to argue with herself, meaning the argument was more or less a decorative factor, a little courtoom she'd built in her head so that whatever she did next could arrive with paperwork. I'm not going, she assertively informed her otherwise insistent mind, but her legs had other plans. And before she knew it, she was standing in the shared bathroom of the second floor brushing her teeth.

\"Not going,\" she muttered under her breath when she entered her bedroom again, falling onto the edge of the bed with a sigh. But her sneakers next to her closed door felt like they were staring at her daringly.

It wasn't long before she'd frustratedly shoved them on her feet, standing in the middle of the pink carpeted room in contemplation. She wanted to go, she knew she wanted to go, and that was the problem with this all.

At one forty one, she turned to face her desk chair. On the back of it hung a black jacket, one that'd been hanging there since Sunday night, slightly too big, and in seventy two hours she hadn't put it on or even thought about doing so, not even in the comfort of her own bedroom with the door shut. It simply lived over there, over the spindle, the way a body lives in a wall. Hyein picked it up once, on Monday, turning to raise her brow at her in question, to which she'd shrugged, not looking up from her textbook on her bed and hummed, \"need to do laundry.\"

\"Uhuh,\" she had retorted in a voice that knew too well.

Now, it was two in the morning, and not a single soul was awake in the building, surely.

The scent of vanilla entered her nostrils before she'd picked it up. She slid her arms through the holes and stood there, in the dark of her own bedroom in a boy's jacket for the first time, the scent coating her in a twist.

\"Okay,\" she breathes to herself, \"whatever\... fuck it, who cares?\"

The hallway, she would find, was the hard part. The floorboards outside Hyein's door had a specific complaint in them, one she'd learned to step over out of pure habit. She'd taken the stairs with her weight on the outside edges, one hand skimming the rail, heart pounding like a robber. On the second landing, she stopped dead, noticing the light at the other end of the hall was on, coming from Danielle Marsh's bedroom.

Of course, her mind snorted, bats are awake at two in the morning, I suppose.

And then she'd went down the last flight faster than she should've, rushing through the entryway and whipping open the front door before her brain could change her mind that this was, in fact, a horrible idea. Turn, lift, pull, and then the early November slapped her across the face with a laugh, the chilling pre-snow weather that was taunting the campus that it would be arriving soon, from the lakes to the west in a coated, freezing white.

It was the coldest night of the year so far, colder than Sunday by a wide margin, the air gone thin and glassy. The porch boards already had frost coming up on them in patches, her breath leaving her in a shove and hanging there. Every lit window on the street had gone dark hours ago, yet she stood there on the steps of the Alpha Phi house five after two in the morning in a jacket that smelled like smoke and vanilla, absolutely certain she was losing her mind.

Then, she shook it off, reminded herself who she was, and went down the steps, starting down the concrete sidewalk of Syracuse University.

To no one's surprise but herself, campus at two in the morning was a place she had never been. She'd been out late, plenty of times, due to those ridiculous parties she kept attending for no particular reason, all of them with the bass still ringing in her ears. But all of those times were an entirely different animal, the tail end of something that still had people in it, stragglers, shouting, a girl crying into a phone on the corner. This was after, there was no Sigma Chi party on a Tuesday night.

Her sneakers scratched against the concrete, the sound almost comforting, echoing through the night air in a symphony with the crickets.

She passed the Language Arts building on the way, not looking up at the roof of it until the impulse took over her.

And the valley, the valley sat where it always had, a wide shallow bowl of the grass in the middle of everything, trees ringed loose around the room. In the daylight, it was arguably the least interesting place at Syracuse. She'd eaten lunch in it with Hyein, Hanni, Minji, or Mark plenty of times, she'd sat in it in September with a textbook open in front of her doing absolutely no reading, watching a boy throw a frisbee badly. There were always people in it, girls lying in the sun, three guys and a speaker, it was the most used piece of ground on the entire campus, which was why she never though of it as anywhere.

Tonight, it was completely empty.

The moon was up over the trees, obnoxiously full, the kind that made the field go silver and blue like someone left a light on. She could see the frost sitting in the grass, crunching under her feet, her own shoes going dark as she stepped off the path down the slope, the cold coming up straight through the canvas.

She walked for a couple of minutes before she saw it, out there in the middle, under the big tree that leaned too far to the right. She'd spent the entire walk assembling a version where she arrived first, stood around aloof, where he didn't show up at all. There were many versions that lived at the back of her brain, because she thought, if he doesn't show, it's easier for me.

But there he was, sitting cross legged on a blanket in the dead center of a field at two in the morning with his hood down, a pair of heavy black headphones over his ears, head tipped back against the trunk, looking up at the sky.

It was clear he'd been there awhile, she could tell by how settled he was in it.

He was going to be out here, something in her chest reminded her, whether I came or not, that's what he said, it's part of his routine.

Her feet carried her across the grass anyway. He didn't turn around, meaning he'd clocked her about forty feet back and had elected, as per usual, not to make anything easy.

\"You're late,\" he hums, not moving a muscle.

\"You didn't give me a time,\" she argues, crossing her arms over her chest to warm up her hands.

\"Two AM,\" he retorts, \"said it twice.\"

\"Yeah, then you hung up on me!\" she cries in exasperation, throwing her hands in the air and slapping them against her sides.

\"Mm,\" he observes, pulling the headphones down to his neck, eyes raking across her body, \"I'm sorry, sweetheart.\"

\"I --- what, why are you apologizing?\"

\"It clearly bothered you.\"

He was being sarcastic, she realized, causing her to glare down at him in annoyance, \"fuck you,\" she snaps at him bitterly. She was trying to be frustrated, but she'd also forgotten what he looked like at night, the moon doing something ethereal and outrageous to his tanned skin, the hoodie, his dark hair falling in his eyes, the whole cool wash of him, into something almost blue.

His eyes kept scanning across her face, until they fell back to her body, onto her shoulders, where a particular jacket was. It took under a second, his expression not moving, in anyway she could've testified to in front of a jury, but something in his shoulders let go about a quarter of an inch, his jaw twitching only gently, though he didn't say a single thing.

But he didn't look away, either.

\"What?\" she pended, trying to see if she could get him to say something about the elephant in the room.

But, naturally, that was never going to work on Haechan. \"Didn't say anything.\"

\"You clearly have something to say.\"

\"Nope,\" he shakes his head a single time, tipping his chin back towards the sky, \"sit down, princess, you're blocking the moon.\"

\"There's a whole field right here---\"

\"---Sit down.\"

She glared at him again but sat down quietly anyway. The blanket was a genuinely ugly thing, dark plaid, thin, the kind that lived in the back of a closet at Sigma for four years being no one's. It also wasn't large enough for two people, meaning that sitting on it involved a negotiation about knees that neither of them were going to acknowledge aloud.

\"This blanket sucks,\" she grumbles, before she'd burst into a chuckle from how dumb this entire thing was.

He turned his head to look at her again, \"is it?\"

\"It's literally like sitting on a napkin.\"

The boy snorted, turning his head towards the field so she didn't see the upwards twitch of his mouth, \"you want the grass?\"

\"I want a better blanket,\" she complained, despite his sassiness, two could always play at that game.

\"You'll survive,\" he monotones, reaching somewhere behind him next to the tree trunk, \"you're a strong girl, aren't you, sweetheart?\"

\"No, apparently not---\"

She was cut off by him plopping a white convenience store bag into her lap, tied at the top in a knot, the condensation already gone off the outside of it. She blinked at him, confused, but he was already looking back up at the sky like nothing had happened.

Opening the bag, she looks down inside, seeing a variety of things; a turkey sandwich, the triangular kind, a bag of hot chips, a package of those small chocolate donuts, a Monster Pink Punch, and perhaps the most odd part of it all, a banana.

Solar pursed her lips, trying to hold back the laugh that so badly wanted to escape her, because technically, this was the first thing he'd ever bought for her. It was an effort, wasn't it? But there was something painfully funny about the hard headed, emotionless, campus heartthrob going to a convenience store in the dark of the night to buy a girl he pretended he didn't know a bunch of crappy food.

It was inevitable, the giggles that started erupting from her. \"What is this?\" she asked in between her laughter, sticking her hand into the bag to pull out the nearly rotten banana, \"why is there a banana?!\"

\"Food,\" he returns, blankly, \"it was by the register.\"

\"Donghyuck, that's location, not a reason,\" she shakes her head, still in fits of giggles, not realizing the name that escaped her lips.

He reached over to take it from her hand at that, peeling it open before holding it back out to her. \"Eat, you didn't eat,\" he mumbles.

Her giggles dissipated then, because there was no correct response to such a thing. He was right, she hadn't ate anything, the reason being that she'd spent her afternoon walking four hundred yards past a stadium to stand at a fence and be quietly dismantled by her own brother, and had come home to lay on her bed in her coat, staring at the wall until it got dark. Nobody in the house had noticed, not exactly, though Hanni had poked her head in sometime around six and chimed, did you eat, Sol? And in response, she'd lied, saying she grabbed something at the dining hall, and Hanni believed her, because she believed her about most things.

\"How\... how'd you know?\" she musters, though it came out quieter than she wanted it to.

\"Hm?\"

\"How'd you know I didn't eat yet?\"

He didn't answer, he just reached back into the bag in her lap to take out the Monster, cracking it open before leaning it against her leg in a position where it wouldn't tip over. \"Just eat, princess.\"

As she would come to learn, he didn't know things about her because he was asking someone, not because he was inquiring, not even researching. He didn't need the internet, or a gossip account, to learn things about her. He just knew them, even before she told him.

Solar didn't say anything else, she just took out the sandwich and ate it with her banana.

It was a terrible sandwich, genuinely, structurally offensive, cold and slightly wet where the tomato had been sitting against the bread. She ate the entire thing anyway in about ninety seconds, sitting cross legged in a frozen field in a boy's jacket, thinking back to a time where food had done something to her, because despite how bad it was, something in her chest twinkled.

There were many things she was trying to work up the courage to ask him, to say to him, beginning with tell me what happened with you and Mark, for real this time, my brother knows it and I don't want to have to ask him, because then he'll say I told you so. She wanted to spout those words evenly without a doubt in her expression, but she knew she wouldn't be able to, because hearing the answer was something she was horrified of.

You'd believe me even less than you should.

Will you ever figure it out? she thought next, the complicated part of this? And then, in retort, her own brain laughed in response, will you?!

No, she frowned, in the cold November night, sitting on a frosted field at sometime past two in the morning.

Even despite everything that had happened, there wasn't any part of her that felt awkward. Her body relaxed before her mind, holding her Monster can in between her cupped hands that were tucked into her lap, crinkling her fingers against it every once in a while just to hear the sound echo through the air.

There were things she could tell him, things she wasn't sure if he would care about, like the fact she was going out with Mark on Saturday.

She was, of course, too afraid to say that, too.

Beside her, Haechan had not moved an inch, he remained frozen next to her with his deep eyes focused on the moonlight. It was like he knew she was having an inner debate with herself and was allowing her to sort it out.

Even in the dark of the night, he seemed to sense that she was staring at him.

\"So,\" he hums, some indeterminate time later, \"did the nerd add you?\"

An undeniable snort escapes from her before she could stop it, covering her mouth with her hand as she chortled into her palm. Haechan, next to her, was looking at her with a blank expression, as if this was a normal question that didn't sound hilarious.

And because she was a brat, she hummed anyway, \"who?\" Entirely casually, she opened the bag of donuts and popped one into her mouth.

\"Mm, cute,\" he returns, knowing every move she was making, tipping his head back against the trunk, \"diamond three.\"

\"Well, I believe his name---\"

\"Don't know his name,\" he cuts her off, \"nor care.\"

\"That's why I was about to tell you,\" she gawks in fake offense, \"I mean, come on, you ruined his life, the least you could do is address him by name.\"

\"You don't know his name either, sweetheart,\" he deadpanned, catching her in her own act, \"nonetheless, some friendly advice won't hurt him.\"

\"Friendly?\" she cries in awe, \"You said aim lower!\"

\"Friendly advice,\" he nods in confirmation.

Solar rounded on him fully, meaning she put a knee on the blanket, and the negotiation about knees was now formally over. \"You humiliated him,\" she pushes further anyway, taking another donut out of the bag and holding it out to him under the moonlight, \"in front of, like, a hundred people, all because he asked me question about Rialto.\"

\"He didn't ask a question,\" he monotones, \"he was looking for a pretty girl that's good at video games to carry him out of shit low.\"

Naturally, mid chewing a donut, Solar pended, \"that's familiar to you, isn't it?\"

He chuckled then, causing her heart to twist, looking down to his feet with his dark hair shadowing his eyes, \"Mm, don't text me at midnight complaining when you drop to Masters.\"

\"I do not text you at midnight!\" she immediately bellows.

\"You texted me at one, actually,\" he ponders, fakely, \"on Sunday.\"

\"I--- that was about practice, that does not fucking count---\"

\"---Oh, I believe you, princess,\" he almost coos, monotonely, a thing she believed only he would ever be able to do, \"I can tell you really mean it.\"

\"Insufferable,\" Solar huffs, grumpily closing her mouth and taking another donut out of the bag.

He leans forward, for a second, reaching his hand forward to likely grab one from the bag. At the sight of it coming towards her, she reaches her hand in first, taking one donut out and chucking it at him. The donut hit him straight in the chest, his eyes looking down at it with his hand underneath it that'd instinctively moved in response to getting something thrown at him.

\"I hate you,\" she mutters.

\"Mhm,\" he pops the donut in his mouth, chewing unnecessarily slowly. His back was against the tree again, the corner of his lips doing a certain thing no one else would ever believe her about. \"You're the one who came out here at two AM though.\"

Her lips formed a straight line and she had to rip her eyes away from him before she spouted something humiliating out.

\"For the moon,\" she informs firmly, \"never seen it full from anywhere other than a penthouse.\"

He couldn't fully retort that, because he knew a part of it was true, and there was an evident buried feeling underneath her words.

\"You haven't missed out,\" he mumbles, \"it's never looked as good as it does tonight.\"

His words caused her to look at him again, wanting to see the way the moonlight made his eyes glisten, as if it would be the last time, to engrave the sight of Haechan --- no, Donghyuck --- when he wasn't so worried about looking composed and unbothered to the world around him. There was something about seeing him for what he really was, a nineteen year old boy who had more passion for music than anything else in his life, who'd had something ripped from his hands and given to someone else, his best friend. His best friend, who he had now barely spoken to, who he had physically fought because of a girl they were both interested in.

Interested in, she felt silly just thinking of it.

Every time she'd ever been near him, it always came attached to something, a party, tournament, fight, a hallway with people on the other side of the wall. Even on Sunday, on the roof, had been a summons with a question in it, she'd gone up that ladder to ask him something specific, and then she climbed back down with an answer in her chest like a swallowed stone.

There were things she was going to say, and not one of them was going to be about what they were or about his addiction or struggles. Tonight, she was going to act like none of those questions existed, even if it wasn't the smartest choice, that's what she would do.

Because, as she realized, before she could approach those things, maybe she needed to know who Haechan Lee really was underneath the mask.

So, she learned things.

She learned that he thought the coffee on this campus was, as he put it, deeply atrocious. It began as a single sentence when she'd mentioned, idly, that she'd gotten an iced coffee from the place near the union on Monday, and he'd lowered his head from the sky again and deadpanned, \"I wouldn't go there again.\"

\"Huh?\" she blinked, \"Why, what could a coffee place have possibly done to you?\"

\"Give me bad coffee,\" he monotones, \"they hold it.\"

She was smiling, like an idiot, because she was so confused and had no idea how to process what she was hearing. \"They what?!\"

\"They brew it in the morning and hold it on a plate all day, sweetheart,\" he informs, blatantly, believing this was casual information she should have known, \"so, by two in the afternoon, you're drinking something that's been cooking for about six hours,\" then he broke their eye contact to lean his head back against the trunk for the hundredth time, \"it's burnt, and they're going to overcharge you for it.\"

Solar put another hand over her mouth so he couldn't see the fact she was having to try so hard to hold in her laughter.

\"Haechan, what --- I have never thought about coffee like that, that's actually kind of impressive,\" she was gawking in between her tiny chuckles that she was swallowing, \"but I'm not gonna lie, it tastes completely normal to me.\"

\"Normal, because you've never had it not burnt.\"

\"We don't even care about coffee that much in the Upper East Side!\" she exclaimed in between giggles.

\"Well, I don't think you want me to tell you what that makes me think,\" he shrugs, \"anyone should know the filtration is---\"

\"The what?!\" She blustered, and the boy seemed to come back to reality, the persona slipping over his face in a millisecond. The brunette sat up straight to peer at him anyway, \"what did you even just say?\" He met her eyes after a second, the blank look back in those irises, \"you said filtration, Haechan.\"

\"I was saying it's fine,\" he deflects bitterly, \"drop it.\"

\"You're a coffee person,\" she practically cheers in delight, \"you're a --- a coffee guy, that's so nerdy, that's like --- almost nerdier than the fact you play Overwatch for fun.\"

\"And what do you play for?\" he raises a brow, unimpressed.

\"A career,\" she sasses with a hand to her heart.

\"Never call me that again,\" he warns, ignoring her comment because he genuinely could not bring himself to attempt to argue.

She learned, additionally, that he could name every person who'd crossed the far path since she'd arrived, which was two, and he'd read out both of them in what felt like such accuracy she'd clapped her hands together and went, \"wait, you might be on point, and I'm never complimenting you again, by the way.\"

The second was a girl walking fast with her arms folded, and he'd gone, \"she just fought with someone, now she's rehearsing what she should've said,\" and the first one had been a guy with a hoodie over his eyes, and he'd hummed, \"he's coming back from somewhere he's going to lie about.\"

\"You will,\" had been his response then.

And she'd learned that the reason he sat on this side of the tree was because the ground stayed wet on the other side, which he delivered in the tone of a man conveying municipal infrastructure. Then, it was that he'd been coming out here since his freshman year, when he knew no one would be looking for him, when he wanted to watch the moon from a different angle, which was how he decided if he'd rather go to the rooftop or here. The main thought that entered her brain was, now I know both of his places.

Did anyone else?

\"Does Jaemin know you sit in a field?\" she'd blurted out the question before she could stop. He'd tilted his head at her, before shaking it, and she'd piped, \"Renjun?\" he shook it again, \"Chenle?\"

\"No, sweetheart.\"

\"Does Mark---\" she started, then stopped herself. The wind brushed through the leaves, knocking a few tiny icicles off the branches that crinkled onto the ground around them.

\"No,\" he clears his throat, \"he doesn't.\"

And Solar, who had learned some things in three months about which doors to lean on and which to walk past, nodded her head a single time, looking to her feet where she played with some frozen grass in front of the blanket, and hummed, \"Huh.\"

Another five minutes passed, and then those five minutes turned into ten. Neither of them needed to say anything, Solar just sat there, shivering under the fabric of a men's jacket, and kept snacking on her donuts.

After she'd nearly ate the entire bag, she embarrassingly folded the top over and set it away from her.

\"I saw my brother today,\" she decides to tell him, needing to get it off her chest, and he was the first person she thought she could tell.

\"Your brother,\" Haechan repeats after a moment of thought, \"willingly?\"

She chuckled, \"yeah, yeah, willingly, I went out to the field,\" she continued, and then, knowing he would ask. \"We got --- uh, we got sent our family schedules,\" she pursed her lips in shame, lowering her head in between her knees, \"my mother's assistant puts them together and sends them, and you have to --- you have to send in a confirmation, there's a deadline.\"

\"When's the deadline?\"

\"The fourteenth,\" she mutters.

Some kind of contemplation flashed through his eyes, but she wasn't looking at him to see it. \"Mm, sounds like you better confirm.\"

\"That's the thing,\" she exhales, \"I just --- don't really want to.\"

\"So, you were asking your brother,\" he states more than asks.

\"Sorta,\" she nods, \"he wasn't of any help, of course, he just told me I better confirm before mother calls me.\"

\"Hm.\"

\"Anyway, he confronted me,\" she continues slowly, \"about the photo, he said someone sent it to him.\"

His eyes narrowed slightly, \"really?\"

\"Yeah, so, she's contacting him directly now,\" she nods with a sigh, \"he doesn't want to tell me who it is.\"

Haechan was quiet for a couple of minutes. \"What else did he say?\"

\"Nothing too different,\" she shrugs, \"same shit, um, about both of you --- how much time I'm spending around you guys\...\" she trailed off, afraid to say the rest of the words. She told herself she wasn't going to get into this tonight.

He watched the way she faltered, he knew why, that there was something she didn't want to say. But he wasn't going to push.

\"He's not going to tell him.\"

\"Huh?\"

\"Your father,\" he confirms, \"he's not going to tell him. If he was, he'd have done it by now, that's what you're worried about, isn't it?\"

\"Um --- partly,\" she mumbles, tripping over her words like an idiot for the second time that night, her brain going in several different directions. Until, she decided, she wasn't going to be able to keep it in. \"He said he spoke to Mark\... about the picture before me, his literal own sister and the person being targeted by that account ninety percent of the time.\"

Beside her, Haechan had grown very still. However, it wasn't the stillness from Media and Society, although it had the same bones. This was quieter, longer, he was looking out at the middle distance of a dark field with his jaw set, eyes moving slightly, the way a person's do when they're reading something that isn't there. And Solar, sat there, pretending she was distracted, but watched him through the corner of her eye, understanding that a great deal was happening about eight inches to her left and that she wasn't going to be explained a single piece of it.

He's doing it again, she thought to herself, back to the way he'd zoned out on Monday after she mentioned Danielle running the accounts.

\"Haechan.\"

\"Uhuh.\"

\"Do you have anything to add?\"

He abruptly snapped his eyes back onto hers.

\"Confirm the travel, pretty.\"

\"What?\"

\"The fourteenth,\" he nodded at her pocket, \"do it now, you'll forget otherwise, then your mother will call you.\"

\"I'm not confirming it at three in the morning!\" she cried, confused how that would even make sense in his brain.

\"You forgot the VOD review.\"

\"I didn't, I just tried to get out of it!\"

\"Well, we both know you're not getting out of this one, are you?\"

She dramatically huffed out into a cloud of air, \"fine,\" she grumbled, whipping her phone out of her pocket right there in a frozen field, spending the next five minutes squinting into the white blast of the screen with her thumbs going, thinking about how he was so irritating yet intoxicating at the same time, while he laid back on the blanket, looking at the moon, and didn't say another thing about it.

The confirmation had been sent at 3:05 AM.

\"There,\" she breathes, shoving the back back into her pocket, \"happy?\"

\"Thrilled,\" he returned without taking his eyes off the sky, \"ecstatic for you, pretty girl.\"

Why is my brother so hellbent on me staying away from you and Mark? I need to know, Haechan, I hate being in the dark.

You could tell me, she thought, you brought me a sandwich and a banana, you could end this in one sentence and go back to looking at the moon like nothing happened.

She opened her mouth, and then she looked at him, at his jaw, the hair in his eyes, the headphones around his neck, the pen gone still in his fingers, and she thought about what asking again would possibly cost her, reminding herself the reason she didn't want to bring any of it up in the first place.

Tonight, she needed to stop thinking about the rumors.

It would be a long time before Solar Lee understood that this was exactly what he had been counting on, and that he'd known it about four seconds before she did.

\-

She rose to her feet at twenty past three, because they'd gone numb and if one of them didn't get up the time would keep passing and the area would begin to populate before either of them expected it to.

Haechan had followed without a word, the two silently gathering all of their things. He put all of the trash into the plastic bag, folded the ugly blanket and tucked it under his arm, and she'd watched him do it casually with her nearly frozen Monster in her hand and wondered what it would be like to see things like this more often.

She had to resist the urge to punch herself.

He walked her to the top of the rise, which was as far as he was going to walk her, a fact they both knew. The path from there ran out to the lit street, the row of houses with porch lights, and neither of them said one word about why he'd stopped there at the tree line. He just did, and she'd halted with him, the two of them standing there in the misty cold.

Rocking on her heels a few times, she finally exhales, \"thanks for the sandwich.\"

\"Mhm.\"

\"It was a really bad sandwich,\" she adds.

\"It was the only sandwich.\"

Her lips formed a straight line, the smile showing on the corner of her mouth anyway, \"I'm just saying, for next time---\" she shut her lips once she heard the words that left it, eyes wide in surprise, and turned a color she was glad he wouldn't be able to fully see due to the darkness.

\"Next time,\" he repeats, noticing the way he did everything, and never missing an opportunity to fluster her.

\"It was hypothetical.\"

\"Right.\"

\"In a general sense type of thing.\"

\"Sure, princess,\" he coaxes, and her knees nearly shook entirely unrelated to the freezing temperature. His eyes raked over her body, head to toe, before he'd hummed, \"keep the jacket.\"

At the subject change, her brows raised in surprise, head looking down at the fabric on her shoulders. \"What, I'm not going to keep your jacket, Haechan.\"

\"I'm not going to take it back,\" he affirms anyway, \"it fits you better.\"

This fits you better than that.

The words echoed in her head like thunder, from a time that felt like years ago, behind the bleachers.

\"Fine,\" she mutters, not wanting him to know that she was secretly happy about this choice.

Though, before she could process what to do next, what would happen next, the boy had reached out in the chill, taking the collar of his own jacket in his fist, pulling her body towards him. Her eyes widened as she processed what was happening, her hands flying up in a defense and landing on his chest, the tee he was wearing under his winter coat, his body somehow faintly warm under the fabric of black.

His lips were soft when they met, a miracle, she would ponder, a boy with soft lips amidst one of the coldest months of the year. It was unbearably slow, no heavy breathing, no pulling of hair, no sucking, nothing that made you feel like it needed to escalate. This kiss was slow, nurturing, the type of kiss that would make someone tear up at the end of a chick flic.

Haechan's other hand came up to the side of her face, thumb going across her jaw, kissing her as if he had no other place on Earth to be.

And nothing else in the entire campus moved.

It was just a gloomy boy's hand on a trending girl's jaw, her hand gripped his wrist under one of his sleeves, afraid to let go. She could feel him smile against her mouth, a sensation shooting through her veins a way she had never felt before, a small sound of near cheer leaving her lips she would forever deny.

When he pulled back, she was breathing a bit more than necessary, her lips tingling as another gust of wind blew past. He didn't step away, their faces were still only inches apart, it would be so easy to just go right back to what they were doing.

Until he'd brushed a strand of hair behind her ear, and his hands fell back into his coat pockets. \"Go inside, pretty,\" he nods in the direction of Alpha, \"that jacket isn't thick enough to be out here this long.\"

\"It's fine, it's really not---\" she started to say, but in the middle of her sentence she visibly shivered.

\"Go home,\" he affirms, \"I'll bring you a better one next time.\"

63: we're all cooked

She'd only got four hours of sleep.

Still, she was handling it the way a person handles something by refusing to acknowledge it and pretending it doesn't exist.

Solar came back through the front door at half past three with her shoes in one hand, the floorboard outside Hyein's room successfully negotiated for the second time in ninety minutes. She'd laid down on top of her comforter, fully dressed, telling herself she was only going to close for a mere second.

This was a lie.

When her alarm went off hours later, she'd been asleep so deeply that the sound arrived from somewhere underwater, causing a shot of electricity to shoot up her spine, jolting her awake. Blinking a few times, her eyes peer up at the pink ceiling of her bedroom for a full minute, trying to come back to Earth and figure out what day it even was.

Like a mist, the scent of fallen leaves and misty winds entered her nose, goosebumps riddling her forearms. The valley, of course. Her mouth still tasted like a Monster she'd finished at three in the morning in a frozen field, which was, a genuinely foul sentence to be true about a person.

She sits up against the headboard, eyes falling on the desk chair, where'd she put a certain jacket at three thirty because she had nowhere else to put it.

And the jacket looked worn. It'd hung there since Sunday looking like an object, flat, folded over the spindle, the shape of something untouched. Now, the sleeves fell differently, collar bent in a way it hadn't been before from where someone's fist had grabbed it and pulled, the whole shape of it gone soft. Anyone who walked into her room would simply see a worn jacket, but she stared at it only to get flashbacks of seventy five minutes in a chilled field.

Frustratedly, Solar threw her feet over the side of the bed, padding across the carpet to poorly attempt to fold the piece of clothing back into the shape it had once been on Monday, smoothing the shoulders flat against the top of her desk, before stepping back to check her work like a woman staging a crime scene.

It didn't work, which she supposed she should've expected.

Eventually, the jacket ended up at the back of her closet behind a coat she never worse. She tried to tell herself she was hiding it for her own good, not because she wouldn't be able to stop thinking about putting it on again.

Deciding that was good enough, she shook her head and headed out of her room to brush her teeth.

The second floor bathroom had Yeojin in it, doing something aggressive to her hair with a round brush. The two of them exchanged the specific nod of people who've agreed not to have a conversation before nine. Downstairs, the house was doing its usual Wednesday, with someone's playlist through a wall, the kettle, a bag of something being shaken out onto a plate in the kitchen, Hanni crying out no, the other one in that kind tone of hers. The whole building smelled like florals and burnt toast, it was almost comforting.

The brunette came downstairs on the outside edges out of pure habit until she noticed she was doing it and tried to appear completely normal. I'm fine, she shrugged to herself, internally, she'd had four hours of sleep, a bad sandwich, and she felt totally fine, buoyant in a way she had no intention of examining.

It's never looked as good as it does tonight.

The tiled kitchen floor was cold against her feet. Hanni, who was at the stove making eggs with Hyein at the island and Yerim next to her, claiming to help, turned her head at the sight of her friend entering.

\"Solar,\" she offered brightly, \"you're up early, do you want some eggs?\"

\"Couldn't sleep that well,\" Solar hums as she slides into the stool next to Hyein, who was already side eyeing her in suspicion, \"sure, Han.\"

\"You need a coffee,\" Yerim chimes from where she was standing.

It bothered her, even though Yerim was utterly harmless and had no intent of saying anything that would do such a thing. Nonetheless, the mention of a girl Solar knew wanted Haechan saying something about coffee lit some kind of fire in her chest that she was struggling to put out.

Filtration, what a stupid word.

\"Yeah,\" she clears her throat, realizing she hadn't said anything in response, \"yeah, I need Dutch Bros.\"

\"Girl, that's way too far,\" Yerim shakes her head, \"you might as well go to that place on campus.\"

\"I don't know, I don't like that place that much,\" she shrugs, biting down on her lip and fidgeting with her fingers in her lap, \"someone told me they mess up the filtration or something.\"

Oh my God.

She should've hit herself over the head.

Yerim blinked at her in confusion, \"the what?\"

\"I didn't know you liked coffee like that, Sol,\" Hanni had hummed innocently, despite the knowing look in her eyes, nearly screaming from how excited she was pretending to be about such a thing.

\"Yeah, I---\"

\"---I totally agree,\" Hyein cried, seeming to put the pieces together herself, seconds after Hanni, \"yeah, that place sucks.\"

And a completely oblivious Yerim looked between the three girls and blustered, \"Wow, I never thought about coffee like that, guys.\"

\"Oh, you should,\" Hanni nodded at her before she changed the subject back to something about the eggs.

Now that she was no longer paying attention, with her back turned, Solar put her elbows on the cold of the counter, burying her face in her hands in utter humiliation. Hyein elbowed her ribs, leaning into whisper, \"dude, are you telling me he's a coffee nerd?\"

With her face still in her hands, the girl only muttered in pain, \"Do not ask me that, Hyein.\"

The girls still didn't know where she was last night, but they seemed to have a pretty good idea that it wasn't in her bedroom.

\"Oh, don't forget,\" Yerim exclaims abruptly, \"sticky note, meeting today!\" she walks across the kitchen to point at the sticky note that was indeed on the front of the fridge.

CHAPTER MEETING 7PM

LIVING ROOMMANDATORY LADIES

Of course, a mandatory chapter meeting was exactly what she wanted to look forward to on a Wednesday, as if the fact she had to actually get up and go to class wasn't enough.

The living room of Alpha Phi at seven on such a day was a different animal than a Sunday afternoon, which Solar had come to learn the way she did most things about the house, by sitting in it and paying attention when she was supposed to be doing anything else. Sunday meetings had bodies in various stages of recovery, Wednesday had homework. Girls came down with laptops balanced on their forearms, highlights in their teeth, someone eating cereal for dinner directly out of the box, Yeojin with a physics packet she was very blatantly not going to finish, the whole room lit yellow and low against a window that'd grown black half past four. Someone turned on the space heater in the corner, resulting in a tick, tick, tick that echoed every ninety seconds.

Solar took her spot on the arm of the far couch, close enough to Hanni to steal her warmth, angled so the room stayed in front of her. Hyein was on the other side of Hanni, snacking on Oreos and talking to no one in particular about her vision for her next design project.

At the front of the room, Chungha stood with her folder and posture, Chaeyeon seated at her right with a pen already out, beginning to run through the agenda how she did everything, briskly, without acknowledging the way half the room was ignoring her. Heejin have a recruitment update, the chore rotation was addressed in the tone of a woman who'd addressed such a thing before. Someone's package had been signed for by someone else, causing a rather heated forty second brief.

Solar merely observed the conversations, tapping the heel of her foot against the couch. Danielle, who had been mostly silent thus far, stood off to the left, near the window, with a folder in her hands that was already open.

She'd been there before anyone, she'd clocked that much walking in, not late this time, early, positioned with her back not quite to the curtains and her weight even on both feet, the specific stillness of a person who'd arrived somewhere with a thing to deliver.

\"Alright,\" Chungha clears her throat, \"before we call the meeting, there are some updates regarding our chapter trip coming up on the thirteenth.\"

Suddenly, every soul in the room sat up straighter. The room's temperature changed instantly, laptops closing, Hyein shooting up so fast she accidentally elbowed Hanni.

\"Updates?!\" someone cried.

\"What happened, did it get cancelled?\" Olivia pipes.

Chungha raises a hand to silence all of the comments, \"no, it did not get cancelled,\" she intones, and everyone subconsciously leaned forward in anticipation. \"So, please, everyone remain calm,\" she urges sternly, raking her eyes across nearly every person in the room, \"Sigma Chi will be joining us.\"

Solar heard it before she processed it. That was the strange part of it all, the sound arriving in the room reaching her before the sentence did, a rising thing that started somewhere near the fireplace and went through the entire living room in about half a second, three separate girls screeching no way in disbelief and bliss, Hyein's hand reaching across Hanni and gripping Solar's ankle hard enough to cut circulation, Yerim placed both her hands over her mouth and silently started screaming.

Sigma Chi is coming with us.

And in the middle of all the noise, Hanni and Hyein both turned to look at Solar in horror, at the exact same time.

Solar looked back at them with the blankest expression she could muster. She'd spent seventeen years learning to do it, but it'd never been this hard.

Hyein recovered first, spinning back around to the room, yelling something about cabins to nobody in particular. Hanni took a beat longer, her eyes doing a small, careful thing, irises soft with concern.

I'm fine, it's okay, Solar mouthed to her. In response, she pursed her lips, turning back to the front despite how unconvinced she was.

\"---four days,\" Chungha had been in the middle of continuing the updates, over the noise and chattering, \"Thursday the thirteenth through Sunday the sixteenth, three nights.\"

\"That's totally different from what you said in October!\" Yeojin cried, not exactly bothered, just surprised at the change.

\"I know,\" Chungha nodded.

\"You said two nights, why did we need the third?\"

\"Well,\" she exhales, \"it became an inter-chapter event with two organizations, a service commitment, and transport for approximately sixty people, at which point two nights stopped being worth the paperwork.\" The girl looks back down at her papers, flipping a page, \"so, it's four days now, cabins --- and before any of you ask, there's a lodge with a dining hall, we'll be doing trail restoration with the conservation group, two work blocks, which is what satisfies this as a service retreat rather than a vacation, and I'd like you all to remember that when speaking to anyone with a title, understood?\"

Most of the room choruses a yes in response.

\"President Lee and I have been working on this for three weeks,\" she continues, closing the portion of the folder.

Solar resisted the urge to snort, President Lee. Her stomach did something slow, unpleasant, thinking about how typical it was that her brother had stood at a fence, four hundred yards past a stadium yesterday evening with a tablet under his arm, telling her she needed to confirm her travel, and failing to say a single thing about the fact he'd just spent three weeks organizing four days of woods for sixty people, including his freshman sister and both of the boys he'd told her to stay away from.

He wouldn't of thought it was worth mentioning, to him, it was logistics.

\"Danielle, if you would,\" Chungha tilts her head in the girl's direction, stepping aside to allow her to have the floor.

Danielle stepped forward immediately, eager to finally have her spotlight, into the space Chungha vacated for her with her folder already open, voice pitched pleasant and clear. Solar sat dead still on the arm of the couch, listening to a girl she couldn't prove anything about acquire authority over ninety six hours of her life.

\"Everything is covered,\" she reports confidently, \"so, no panicking about dues, ladies. The fund successfully absorbs the site and food, and Sigma will be covering transport and half of the equipment. I'll need a headcount by Friday because we're charged per bed afterwards,\" she turns a page without looking down, \"there will be an inventory sheet on the fridge. If you own a sleeping bag rated below thirty, a lantern, camp stove, or a cooler, write it down, it would be a great help, and if you're driving, I'll need to know your car and seats.\"

\"Jeez,\" Olivia muttered, \"girl is serious.\"

She wasn't wrong. Danielle Marsh had conveniently made herself the person who knew who was sleeping where, who was riding with whom, what everyone owned, what it costs, and she'd done it so competently, so usefully that a room of thirty girls audibly exhaled sighs of relief. Nobody hands a treasurer that, a treasurer takes it, one line item at a time, while people are grateful.

She hadn't looked at Solar.

\"Now, are there any questions on budget?\" Danielle hummed.

\"Are there showers?\" Yerim raised her hand.

\"There are showers,\" Chungha confirmed.

\"Thank God,\" she breathes, falling back against the cushion with her hand on her chest. The room went briefly silent, before she'd piped again, in a voice pitched exactly loud enough, \"so, are all of them coming, or like---\"

\"Yes,\" Chungha nods, without inflection.

Yerim turned and exchanged glances with several of the girls, who all seemed to be aware of her apparent crush on a certain member. Her eyes fell onto Hyein, Hanni, and Solar, likely recounting their kitchen conversation, face lit up with pure excitement. Hyein had sent her a smile, Hanni a thumbs up, before they'd looked back to Solar with eyes that said everything.

Four days.

Her eyes stared at a spot on the carpet. Yerim had asked her to introduce her to Haechan, she'd said she wasn't with either of them, on the record, to a girl who commonly had lunch with Danielle Marsh, and thought at the time, this is clever.

But now, that same girl would a clear shot at him in a forest for four days, and Solar couldn't object. She'd personally removed her own standing to object, nonetheless all of the other factors. Her brother was there, Mark was there, the girl who ran the gossip accounts would be there, watching every move she made with her camera ready.

Biting the inside of her cheek, she reaches down to press her thumb into the meat of her own palm until it burned.

\"Lastly, we have already spoken to all extracurricular heads and informed them of the trip, so do not fret on missing anything important,\" some of the girls cheered in gratefulness. Chungha tucked her folder under her arm, \"that's all, girls, remember --- waivers this week, don't make me chase you.\"

Then, the room came apart into noise, Hyein already loudly assigning cabin arrangements that weren't hers to assign, Olivia demanding to know the drinking policy, and being told flatly by Chaeyeon that there was one. Somebody dragged the space heater to a different corner where it would tick at a different interval.

Solar stayed on the arm of the couch, mind running rancid.

Once most of the girls were gone, Hyein spun around, grabbing her knees with both hands. \"Four days,\" she hissed under her breathe, eyes enormous, \"four days, Sol, in the woods, with---\"

\"---I know, Hyein.\"

\"I'm just saying!\"

\"You're always just saying.\"

\"And I'm always right!\" she declares, releasing her knees and standing up to continue her cabin campaign in the other room.

\"I hope this is quick,\" Jisung had already been whining, on a Wednesday afternoon, as if he ever had anything better to do.

Renjun had gotten there early, since being early meant getting the end of the couch that wasn't broken. Jisung plopped onto it next to him, holding a bag of chipshe was eating one at a time with an unbearable amount of crunch. Chenle entered at half past one, laptop under his arm, with the expression of a man being detained.

He didn't say anything as he took one of the chairs, eyes narrowed down at the screen in concentration. The sounds of Overwatch briefly filled the room, making it evident he was deeply engrossed in reviewing scrims.

Slowly but surely, the room began to fill with various boys, some pretending they cared about the meeting, and many hungover or presently under the influence despite it being a Wednesday. Jeno and Jaemin came in from the kitchen, their cheeks red with heat, showcasing the fact they too were indeed intoxicated at half past one on a Wednesday.

And Mark, Mark came in last, looking decent, which Renjun noticed, eyes following his movements carefully. His hair was done, he shockingly wasn't looking down at his phone, and he'd casually dropped onto the arm of the couch, greeting about four people individually.

Haechan was already there, he'd been there even before Renjun, in the chair by the window, headphones around his neck, one leg over the other, isolated from everyone yet close enough to hear all of it, which was the exact same six square feet of that room he'd been sitting in since freshman year.

Finally, Jaehyun entered with Yuta, carrying a stack of papers, and the room immediately rearranged to act as if it'd been behaving.

\"Pay attention,\" he firmly addresses them all, \"and this will end quickly.\"

\"No it won't,\" Jisung mutters.

\"Jisung.\"

\"My bad!\"

\"The trip has been confirmed,\" he announces, and before he could get another word out, the room of thirty boys erupted into yells. Jeno jumped to his feet, standing up off a couch for a camping trip like a man hearing his own name at the draft, both hands in the air, roaring a bunch of tipsy incoherence. Jaemin was howling, claiming he was going to be on the prowl, and Jisung's chips went across the carpet in a wide, beautiful arc that no one was going to willingly pick up.

\"---it will be a joint trip with Alpha Phi,\" he informs over the noise, \"which I notice some of you have already figured.\"

The room grew slightly quieter.

\"Holy fuck,\" Jeno was gawking, \"in the woods for four days with a bunch of women,\" he turns to Jaemin, dramatically slapping his arm over and over, \"pinch me, bro, am I dreaming?\"

\"Sit down, Jeno,\" Jaehyun demanded.

Knowing it was never a good idea to disobey the president, he obliged.

Jaemin had been sitting there on the couch with a smirk on his face, clearly having known all along, since he was the social chair. Renjun narrowed his eyes at him, accusing flatly, \"you did this, didn't you?\"

He turned to him with that same insufferable expression, \"perhaps I did, Renjun.\"

Renjun didn't get to say anything else, because Jaehyun continued running through the rest of the important information. \"There will be a service component, trail restoration, two work blocks.\"

And the entire room groaned in genuine agony, an ancient sound from a bunch of boys that had never done a millisecond of actual service work in their lives.

\"You'll survive,\" he deadpans, \"transport's split, we'll be covering half the equipment, Alpha's treasurer is running the vehicle list and site inventory, so if you'll be driving, let her know.\"

No one noticed except Renjun, due to per luck, the way that Haechan's face made the tiniest slip of an expression. His head didn't turn, eyes didn't move, but there was something underneath brewing.

The meeting would wrap up ten minutes later, with a final warning for Jaehyun that this was their chance to get on the dean's good side again, since Alpha was such a highly respected sorority. Everyone muttered something about trying their best or giving an attempt before the living room emptied.

Renjun went out the side door to light a cigarette, his third of the day. The side steps at Sigma were cold, narrow, facing nothing but the neighbors fence. November had gotten properly serious in the last week, he could see his own breath before he'd even lit anything.

Haechan was sitting on the bottom step.

\"You're in my spot,\" Renjun observes, sitting on the step above him to take out his cigarette. For a while, neither of them said a thing.

Inside, through the screen door, someone was yelling about sleeping bags.

\"They're disgustingly excited about the woods,\" he mutters, \"just because they know they're going to sneak in pounds of alcohol.\"

\"Not wrong,\" Haechan nonchalantly acknowledges, despite the fact he was one of the people who would indeed be doing that.

\"You're not, though.\"

Haechan turned his phone screen over in his hand, not saying anything in response.

Renjun smoked, letting the silence overcome them for a second, staring ahead at the fence, mind wandering back to how he'd been in that house for a year. He'd gotten fairly good at knowing which silences were nothing. Haechan not talking during a meeting wasn't anything out of the ordinary, he'd spent entire semesters being too hungover or drugged out to process what anyone was saying. Nonetheless, he was someone that could rarely avoid the temptation to say clever things or make fun of one of them, it was just what he tended to do. So, it was still odd when he'd sat there entirely silent the entire time.

\"Four days is a long time,\" Renjun thinks aloud.

There was a pause that went on a beat too long to be meaningless.

\"Just four days,\" Haechan shrugs.

He finished his cigarette then, putting it out against the concrete before rising to his feet. Haechan didn't react nor move, too engrossed in staring out at the fence, headphones still around his neck, phone still face down on his knee like a man waiting for something he had no intention of admitting he was waiting for.

Renjun didn't have to think too hard about the fact this was all going to somehow turn into a nightmare. And he, was one of the two boys in the house who realized this, who'd paid enough attention to the two boys to put the pieces together. Him and Chenle were the only people who could see it laying in front of them, yet they didn't have the slightest idea of how to fix it.

He was beginning to think, such a thing was just inevitable.
