Haechan was already in his seat when she arrived to Media and Society.

Solar drops into the chair beside him without saying a word, taking out her notebook and opening it to a clean page, followed by a pen. Immediately, she started drawing stars in the margins as another poor attempt to distract herself.

He didn't touch her a single time in the seventy five minutes of the lecture, not the back of her chair, her ankle under her desk, not the thing he'd done on Monday where his hand lingered on her thigh for the entirety of the second half of the lecture whilst he took the most absurdly clean notes. Thursday, he sat with both feet flat on the floor and both hands on his own desk like a boy in a brochure.

It annoyed her.

First, she spent the beginning twenty minutes pissed off about it, then the second twenty minutes annoyed with herself for being upset about it. And by the time it'd gotten to the last thirty five, she finally began to process the fact he knew exactly what he was doing.

The professor released them at ten past two, the hall emptying nearly at once, a hunded people standing up. The scraping and shuffling of their chairs echoing through the high ceilings. Solar hesitantly pushed her chair back, rising to her feet to pack her own bag.

Haechan hadn't moved a muscle, like he was waiting for the inevitable. Slowly, the room around them drained, leaving two people sitting perfectly still as Solar finished zipping up her bag. The door swung heavy and slow on its hinge for the last time.

She pursed her lips, debating with herself internally, until her mind wandered back to the chilly air on the night of a full moon, and she sighed, \"Mark texted me.\"

He'd turned in his chair to face her then, elbow hooked over the back of it, something behind his eyes doing a small unimpressed thing at such a name.

\"About the trip,\" she added, when he didn't immediately respond.

\"Alright, I'm sure he's excited.\"

\"It's not about that,\" she snaps in frustration, \"you've known for way longer than I have, and you didn't think to say something about this?!\"

He tapped his knuckles against the back of the chair a few times, not shocked that she'd put the pieces together, whether Mark told her or not. \"It was officially announced today,\" he corrects blankly, \"everyone just guessed last meeting that Jaemin was trying.\"

\"Shouldn't you of mentioned that?!\" she whisper yells, \"You know, the fact we're going to be stuck in the woods for four days with my brother, Mark, and Danielle?!\"

Haechan stared at her for a couple of minutes. For once, he seemed to be thinking carefully about his next words.

\"We're careful,\" he monotones finally, \"it's not that serious, sweetheart.\"

Solar heaves out a sigh, \"Haechan.\"

\"It's not,\" he insists anyway, \"I didn't tell you because I'm not worried about it.\"

\"Okay, that doesn't change the fact this is insane, what am I going to do if Jaehyun sees me with either of you?!\" she complains, \"Or if Danielle gets some stupid photo of us\...\" she trails off, not knowing how to end the sentence, turning and looking at the ceiling, her hands flying into her hair and pulling out of stress.

\"Princess,\" Haechan urges, \"you're overthinking it,\" he assures her, almost soft, \"but I understand why you're upset I didn't tell you.\"

She turns back to him abruptly. \"You understand?\"

\"Mm,\" he nods, \"I should've, but we're not going to get caught, pretty.\"

Wow, she thought in utter bewilderment, he's agreeing with me for once.

And she had no idea what to do with that, Haechan agreeing with her felt totally foreign. She was realizing, nonetheless, that he was very different from the person everyone painted him as, he was simply scared.

Somebody's music went past in the corridor and faded.

She couldn't blame him for it, was the thing. He was afraid of what this could mean.

She was, too.

So, she closes her eyes and exhales deeply. \"Okay, it's --- yeah, we just don't do anything stupid,\" she tells herself, more than him, \"I just have to relax and keep my distance.\"

\"Mm,\" he hums, \"sounds like a great plan.\"

\"It is,\" she huffs.

\"Come here, sweetheart,\" he deadpans.

Before she could process such a demand, he'd reached out to grab both of her wrists with either hand, tugging until she nearly stumbled onto his lap, both of her legs on either side of him, crushed in the tiny chair that was not meant for two people. She'd squealed in shock when he did so, but her body seemed to let it happen.

\"So annoying,\" she bitterly mumbles, despite the fact she was allowing his face to be inches away from hers, failing to move a single muscle.

\"It'll be okay, pretty,\" he whispers, teeth gently biting her earlobe, sending tickles up her spine, \"is that what you wanted to hear?\"

\"Shut up,\" she whines, pushing his face away from her ears, \"you know, you've already been getting me in trouble again.\"

\"Again, huh?\"

\"Yes!\"

\"And how about Marky?\" he raises a brow, sassily, \"You're telling me it's not concerning the way he brags about you all over his Instagram?\"

\"Well,\" she pauses, \"yeah, Jaehyun wasn't happy about that, either.\"

He already knew that of course, she'd already told him, but he was being difficult on purpose.

\"I don't think I'm the problem then, am I?\" he lowly mumbles, \"Seems to me like you quite like it when I do this,\" his lips slowly hovered over her neck, before they'd leaned down far enough to suck on the skin.

\"Haechan,\" she curses, pushing his face off of her again, his teeth tugging on the skin of her neck when she did so, \"that's not what I meant, anyway,\" she grumbles, \"I mean that I said the word filtration in my kitchen!\"

And Donghyuck Lee did something she didn't see coming, the corners of his mouth twitched, and he started snickering. Apparently, this was one of the rare hilarious things to him, from a boy who rarely found anything worth grinning about.

\"Why are you laughing?!\" she sasses, \"You do realize absolutely no one says that, right?!\"

\"That's not true,\" he finally monotones.

\"It is entirely true!\"

\"There's an entire discipline, sweetheart---\"

\"---a discipline, seriously!\" she spouts in disbelief, putting both of her hands on his chest and gently shoving him to release some of her annoyance.

He was chuckling again. It was far from the flat scrape he used on people in hallways, but a short involuntary giggle she had heard only once before.

\"They clocked me,\" she admits, trying to shove away the fact such a sound was impacting her more than she wanted to face, \"four seconds, Hyein asked me if you were a coffee nerd.\"

\"And?\" he rose a brow in question.

\"I --- put my face in my hands.\"

\"Mm, effective strategy,\" he hums, laying his forehead on her shoulder, his arms slowly wrapping around her waist, \"that's good, princess.\"

\"It's not good---\"

\"Sure it is.\"

\"They're unbearable, Hyuck, they were already unbearable in the first place after Halloween, and now they know you have these opinions about something as minimal as---\"

The nickname slid off her tongue before she could stop it, the one only Mark had ever really used. The second it left her, his head jerked, eyes locked onto her irises hard enough she would've fallen over if he wasn't holding onto her.

\"Say it again.\"

\"Say what\...\" she hesitates, the realization slapping her in the face, \"oh, oh my God.\"

\"It's not bad,\" he smirks, \"it's nice coming from your lips.\" His hand reached up to run his thumb across her bottom lip.

\"Stop,\" she hushes, slapping his wrist until his fingers fall to her jaw instead, which she decided was acceptable, \"you're insufferable.\"

\"Mhm.\"

\"Genuinely, you're the worst person I've ever had the displeasure of knowing.\"

\"You're the one who continues to sit here, pretty girl.\"

\"Assigned seating.\"

\"There's no assigned seating,\" he snorts.

\"Assumed,\" she corrects, though her voice was barely a whisper.

He hummed in acknowledgment, seemingly allowing her a break. The corridor grew quiet behind the walls. Somewhere below, a door opened and closed, someone laughing about something on a lower floor of the stairs, the winter light through the high windows going the flat grey they went at two in the afternoon of November. Slowly, she became far too aware that she hadn't thought about Danielle Marsh, her brother, or a camping trip in eleven minutes.

\"Four days,\" she thinks aloud, \"in the woods, with all of them in cabins,\" she starts giggling from how dumb it sounded, \"this seriously does not sound real.\"

\"Uhuh,\" he monotones, hand sliding down to her neck, fingers tickling the soft of the skin. His fingers gradually began to wrap around the small of it, \"what --- you don't like the idea of being alone in the woods with me for four days, sweetheart?\"

Her eyes snapped to him instantly, cheeks burning in seconds. And Haechan, he was looking at her with absolutely nothing on his face, meaning he'd said something so irritably stupid on purpose.

\"We both know that's not what I said.\"

\"Didn't say it was.\"

\"Nor is it what I meant, anyway!\"

\"Mm,\" he nods, \"sure sounded like it.\"

\"You're --- it's literally a deliberate misreading of a reasonable complaint about group housing---\"

\"Sure, princess,\" he lowly drawled, fingers tightening around her neck, only enough to cause her spine to tense.

\"Stop saying sure like that.\"

\"Like what?\" he pends teasingly. Solar was so busy being outraged that she almost forgot what he was so clearly doing, as his other hand slowly crept to clench her waist.

\"You know,\" he mutters, \"room's empty till two thirty.\"

\"Okay,\" she huffs, \"why would I need to know that?\"

Still, she felt it instantly, the heat starting low in her stomach and spreading outward, until her thighs tighten around the narrow metal frame of the chair. His hand is still at her neck, thumb resting against the hinge of her jaw, pulse ticking under the pad of it. The other had found the soft place just underneath her hipbone, under the hem of her sweater, fingers spread warm against bare skin. But he didn't move any of them, he was simply waiting for something he already knew the answer to.

\"Twenty minutes,\" she acknowledges in a whisper.

\"Nineteen now,\" he hums, mouth centimeters from hers, the faint scent of mint and the colder edge of whatever he'd been drinking earlier hitting her in a wave, \"you counting?\"

\"Calculating risk, maybe.\"

\"Cute,\" he snorts, the corner of his mouth lifting the tiniest amount. He shifts under her, enough that she feels him hard against the seam of her jeans, a breath she didn't realize she was holding hitching in her throat. The sound causing him to tilt his head, hot air fanning her chin, \"there she is,\" he lowly teases.

\"Do not.\"

\"Do not what?\"

\"Do not look at me like that when we're in a fucking lecture hall, Haechan!\"

He glances past, over her shoulder a single time. The fluorescent lights overhead hum steadily. Somewhere deeper in the building, a radiator loudly ticks. \"Door's closed, hall's dead, and you're the one on my lap, princess.\"

\"You pulled me,\" she hisses.

\"Still here, aren't you?\" His hand leaves her neck only long enough to catch the back of her head to push her towards him, closing the last inch of space between them. The kiss was nothing close to careful, it was hungry, open mouthed, almost more vile than the Halloween hallway, full of all the things they hadn't done then and couldn't seem to stop thinking about. She tasted the mint, the faint metallic edge of the cold classroom air still on his lips, her fingers digging into the collar of the hoodie until the fabric bunches.

Haechan makes a low sound against her mouth, his hand still at her hip sliding higher, under her sweater, palm flat against the bare skin of her waist. Her body trembles with electricity, arching into the touch without meaning to. The chair creaks under the shift of weight. Below, a locker slams, both of them freezing for half a second before the silence returns, somehow thicker than before.

\"Donghyuck,\" she half urges and pleads, completely conflicted.

The word only made him grip her harder, \"fuck,\" he grumbles under his breath. His lips smash onto hers harder, the hand under her sweater moving up until his thumb brushes the underside of her bra. The underwire tugs for a second before he pushes the cup up, finding the soft weight of her breast, fingers rolling the nipple until her hips rock once against him without permission. The friction of denim against denim is sharp and painfully insufficient.

\"Someone could---\"

\"Shh,\" he hushes, \"they won't.\" He said the words against her throat, teeth scraping the place he already marked, the skin still tender. \"And if they do, you'll look at them the way you're looking down at me right now, I'm sure they'll regret what they walked in on, or maybe not.\"

He was so irritating.

She hated how much she liked it. She knew she should climb off, fix her clothes, and walk out into the November grey like a person with somewhere else to be. Instead, she reaches between them, pressing her palm to the front of his jeans, feeling the shape of him under the denim, the heat of him already soaking through it, watching his eyes nearly go half lidded before he recovered.

\"You're not very good at keeping distance,\" he teases, almost fond.

\"You're worse,\" she bitterly retorts, words slurred from the way his hands were roaming her body.

He was smirking against her neck, hands sliding down to undo the buttons of her jeans, the zipper following with a soft metallic rasp that clicks against the empty room. It'd taken her four minutes. That was the part she didn't think about, standing at her vanity at half past five, hair pushed over one shoulder and the little sponge going in small, practiced circles under her jaw. Four minutes, possibly five, and she didn't have to squint or turn her head under the light, she just did it, the way one ties their shoe.

Two weeks ago she'd sat in that exact chair for twenty minutes with her mother's voice in her head telling her she was blending too harshly. Now, she capped the tube, pulling a turtleneck of her head, and went to practice.

The gaming lab was already glowing when she pushed through the doors, RGB blooming warm against the dark of the hallway, the hum of PCs arriving before the room did. Olivia was arguing with a monitor, Haerin had her hood up, and Doyoung was standing at the front with his notebook, doing the thing where he looks at the block and then all of them, which was his version of a greeting.

\"Regions is in twenty six days,\" he announces, \"does anyone want to guess how many of those are practice days?\"

\"Please don't make us guess,\" Olivia monotones.

\"Fourteen.\"

\"Then why did you ask---\"

\"---Warm up,\" he cuts her off with a raise of his hand, before turning around.

Solar giggled to herself, sitting down at her setup and slipping her headset on.

It was an amazing practice. That was the thing no one warned you about, that things could be great sometimes with no strings attached. Her Kiriko was fast, calls clean, she read flanks before they happened. Somewhere in the third scrim, she stopped narrating her own performance in her head and simply played, which was the only version of herself she'd never had to actually perform.

\"Sol,\" Minji was gawking, delighted, \"that was fucking insane --- how do you even do that?\"

\"That was a read,\" Solar shrugs, cockily.

\"That was witchcraft.\"

\"Actually, it was more like film study---\" She put one of her fingers up, pushing pretend glasses up her nose.

\"You do not watch film,\" Minji bitterly retorts, gently shoving her shoulder with her own.

\"Sure I do!\"

\"Name one,\" she dares, and Solar immediately faltered, Olivia catching the tail end of the conversation and snickering so hard she had to mute herself in comms.

Doyoung let them go at eight, the room emptying as chairs echoed, everyone talking at once about nothing in particular. Olivia was already narrating a play she'd made forty minutes ago as thought it'd aged into legend.

Solar was unplugging her headset when she noticed Chenle staring at her. He was two seats down with his hoodie half over his head, laptop under his arm, face entirely empty. But his eyes were locked onto her face half a second longer than a person holds a look at someone they see four times a week.

\"What?\"

\"Nothing,\" he shrugs, focusing down on his bag.

\"You were just staring at me,\" she accuses.

\"I stare at plenty of things,\" he informs, zipping his bag and throwing it on his shoulder, \"you're simply a creature I stare at.\"

\"A creature?\" she deadpans, \"seriously?\"

\"Yep,\" and then, he left the room without another word.

\"He is wild,\" Minji was snorting beside her, and Solar only shook her head in disbelief as the two left the labs, the last ones, as always.

Outside, it was freezing. It hit them the second they opened the doors, that thin glassy cold that came off the lakes before snow did. Minji said something unrepeatable about it, pulling her sleeves down over her hands, and the two of them began down the path with their shoulders almost touching the way they always did.

\"So, my mom called me,\" she shares.

\"Oh no.\"

\"Oh yes,\" she sighs dramatically, \"an hour, Sol, an hour.\"

\"About what?\"

\"How I don't call her,\" Minji snorts, \"which, if you think about it---\"

\"---is self-solving?\" Solar guesses, and Minji beams, pointing at her without looking over, which was the highest form of agreement she offered.

The two kept walking with no cares in the world, seemingly. Someone's music came out of an open window. Minji told her about a film seminar where a boy had used the word auteur eleven times, and Solar told her about Yeojin's physics packet, to which the girl laughed that she'd pay real money to watch someone like Yeojin fail physics. It was so easy it was almost embarrassing, the way they flowed with no effort.

\"How about the trip?\" she hums finally, at they round a corner, hands in the pockets of her jacket.

The remembrance of such an event caused her to exhale deeply, the white cloud hovering in front of their faces. She spent the next few minutes briefing Minji on the majority, omitting details she simply thought she didn't want to know the full of, the meeting, four days, cabins, thirty boys and thirty girls in the woods with a service project stapled to it. Minji listened to every word, making appropriate noises of horror in the right places.

\"That's --- good God,\" she muttered.

\"Oh, that's not all,\" Solar rose a hand, \"Danielle is running it, too.\"

\"Huh?\"

\"She stood up at that meeting with a folder that was clearly already open,\" she complains, \"by the time she sat down, she had the budget, headcount, equipment list, you fucking name it --- she knows where every single person is sleeping for four days and she got it in ninety seconds, and they all sat there and clapped for her.\"

Minji didn't say anything at first. They walked past the flickering lamppost.

\"That's bad,\" she finally deadpans.

\"Gets worse,\" Solar huffs, \"I saw my brother, Tuesday.\"

And then, before Minji even probably got to process the last tidbit, Solar told her about Tuesday evening, that someone, blatantly Danielle, sent Jaehyun the Halloween photo, and that in return, he'd gone to Mark before coming to her.

\"Fuck,\" she breaths, \"that is worse, she really sent it to him like she was the nice one letting him know what's going on.\"

\"Yep,\" she chuckles bitterly, \"it's sick.\"

\"And then he asks Mark,\" she repeats slowly.

\"Yup.\"

Minji walked about six more steps without saying anything else. But Solar could feel it, the shape of it, all three pieces sitting on the table in front of her at once, a line running clean between them. How unfortunate it was that she didn't know the dark truth behind it all.

\"That's messed up,\" the girl voices into the quiet, \"I'm sorry, Sol.\"

Solar bit her bottom lip to stop herself from smiling, bumping her shoulders into hers, a grateful gesture, because Minji never did the thing everyone else did. There was something restful about a person that didn't make it their mission to solve you.

\"How are you?\" she'd asked her instead.

\"Bored,\" Minji hums, \"I've watched four hours of scrim VODs and lived off of pop tarts, I have nothing interesting to report,\" she giggles, before her voice grows serious again, \"hey, I've noticed you checking your phone like a Victorian widow, by the way.\"

Her sudden words made Solar's eyes bulge. \"What?!\"

\"You checked it twice during warmups,\" Minji teased, \"I'm guessing that's why Chenle kept staring at you.\"

\"It was Hanni!\"

\"It was not.\"

\"It's not serious,\" Solar deflects. It came out easy, level, the same sentence she'd given Yerim in a living room and Hyein in a kitchen, fitting in her mouth like something she'd made.

In reality, four hours ago she'd been in his lap in an empty lecture hall, calling him a name that had never belonged to her, and he'd asked her to say it again.

\"Uhuh.\"

\"You clearly don't believe me,\" Solar mentions with a sigh.

\"I didn't say anything,\" Minji shrugs casually, \"I always believe you, Sol.\"

She hated how true it was, because Minji had a big heart. She may see through it, but she would always see the good in Solar, even when she couldn't see it herself.

It'd been the easiest hour of her whole week.

Oh jeez.

"Yeah, of course, let's go," Solar exhales, forcing a smile on her face and grabbing Yerim's wrist. She sends Hanni a short wave before beginning to walk across the living room of the fraternity house.

It was the part she'd think about later, no one pushed her to do it, no one was watching except Hanni, and Hyein who had returned with drinks for them. She crossed the room with a sorority sister on her arm at an entirely normal pace while the bass vibrated the walls and sweaty bodies collided around them.

He saw them coming from about twelve feet out, and she watched him do it, the exact instant he put two and two together, which took him no time at all. Nothing changed about him other than the fact he took his hand out of his pocket, eyes narrow as he continued to sip his drink.

He's going to enjoy this, she thought bitterly, he already fucking knows, and he's going to rub it in my face on purpose.

"Haechan," Solar greets fakely, her voice level, "I wanted to introduce you, this is Yerim, and Yerim, this is Haechan."

It was taking everything inside of her to keep that smile on her face, which was something Solar Lee had never had trouble with in her entire life.

"Hi\!" Yerim practically cries, before placing a hand over her mouth in embarrassment from how loud it came out.

Haechan's eyes slowly went from Solar onto the girl next to her, who looked like she was going to crumble from nerves. "Yerim," he returns monotonely, "pleasure."

Then, he says nothing else, long enough that Yerim's smile started to do something uncertain at the corners. Solar felt her own stomach drop about an inch, thinking he was perhaps going to be mean to a nineteen year old girl in cat ears. But more so, at the fact she wouldn't entirely hate him doing that.

What was wrong with her?

Until he tips his head about ten degrees and hums, "cat's good."

"Really?\!" Yerim boasts brightly, realizing what he meant.

"Mm, very committed," he nods towards her ears, "most of these people didn't bother despite the rules."

"I know right\!" she gawked, "It's literally in the post, Jeno said wear it or don't—"

"—That's Jaemin's," he deadpans, "Jeno can't form a sentence to save his life."

Yerim giggled like he'd done a bit, which technically, he sort of had. And Solar, Solar stood there approximately fourteen inches to his left and watched him be charming. She watched him do what he was known for doing around here, since the day he'd come to this campus, and felt something twist at the bottom of her chest.

He wasn't warm, he was doing the thing he did at the beginning of a semester with a room of prospective members, the thing that was his job in this house, attention deployed in small measured amounts, a question every third beat, the flat delivery reading as dry rather than uninterested to anyone who hadn't spent months deciphering the difference.

"What year are you?"

"Um, technically a sophomore," she pipes, "I transferred, barely, it's kind of a whole thing—"

"—What are you studying?"

"Comm," she continues, genuinely thrilled that he was asking her things.

All she could do was stand there and listen to him make this girl think that he cared about every word she was saying to him. He didn't look at her once, and she hated the fact she knew he was aware of exactly where she was, watching him hold a cup at exactly the same angle for ninety seconds.

He isn't going to look at me, and that's the whole thing, isn't it?

Perhaps, the most bitter part of it all was that she couldn't leave. She'd made the introduction, walking away thirty seconds into it would say something, though standing there said something else. There was no arrangement of her body in that room that meant nothing, and she'd built the room herself, on Monday.

Although, she had also leaned across a desk in a lecture hall and given a stranger her Battletag on purpose, in front of a hundred people, to make a point to a boy that wasn't supposed to care.

She'd also had this same boy bend her over that same desk.

She wanted to slap herself from thinking about it.

"—so, do you have his number already?" Yerim had turned to her, nervous, speaking barely a whisper because she was feeling shy, "I asked Hyein and she said she doesn't have it, then I thought wait—"

"—She doesn't," Haechan cut in, hearing every muffled word she was saying, "nobody does."

Then, he reached over, taking the phone she was holding straight out of her hand. Yerim made a small noise of surprise as he typed into it one handed, cup still held low against his thigh in the other.

"Are you for real?\!" she was crying as he handed it back to her, her eyes peering down at the contact.

"Mhm."

"Oh my God," she was screeching under her breath, turning to Solar with bulging eyes.

And Solar stood there and forced a small smile on her face.

It was funny, objectively, extremely funny. If it'd happened to anyone else, she'd laugh. He'd spent two months not answering people, she'd watched him ignore three separate girls at a party a week ago, pull his arm out of one of their hands without looking. He wasn't someone who gave out anything, and he'd just handed his phone number to a girl he'd known for four minutes without hesitation, in front of the one person on campus who understood what it cost him.

Which was zero, because he would never answer a text from Yerim. It costs him absolutely nothing.

"Do you want a drink, Yerim?" Solar yelled at her over the music, deciding she couldn't stand to witness this anymore but not wanting to show it on her face.

"Prob, but hold on\!" she exclaims, eye catching something. Then, in delight, she turns and grabs something by a plastic cauldron next to the wall, before turning around with two red devil horns.

What a fucking joke.

"Okay, so, you had them on last week," she hurriedly explains.

"Yerim," Solar calls out to her, a last ditch effort.

But the girl already went on the tip of her toes, and Haechan tipped his head down about an inch, which he had to do since she was shorter and the alternative was making her fall in front of people. Yerim slid the band into his hair with the enormous care of someone handling something borrowed, before stepping back to admire it, a proud smile taking over her face, and a cluster of girls somewhere behind them made noises of genuine joy at the sight.

The horns sat crooked in his dark hair, one of them knocked slightly off centre, the way they'd been a week ago in a hallway on the second floor of this house, at the exact moment she'd stopped being able to breathe properly.

Then his eyes fell on her, for the first time in six minutes, over the top of a girl's head.

"Drinks\!" Yerim cheers, turning to Solar and already heading in the direction of their friends, "Let's find Hyein and Hanni\!"

She'd clearly assumed Haechan was going to follow, like the two were soul bonded since he'd given her his number. Little did she know, he was, but for an entirely different reason. Still, the girl didn't notice as she started prancing away in search for the two girls, far too caught up in her own excitement.

So, it'd left him to slowly walk up to her. She'd only sent him a glare, spinning on her heel and starting towards the same direction.

Of course, he'd followed.

"Sweetheart," he hums, lowly, bending over so his voice carried into her ears, "you want a drink, don't you?"

She didn't respond. There wasn't a version of answering him that didn't make it worse, so she kept her head high and continued walking.

The living room had gotten to the stage of the night where it no longer resembled that of a room. Bodies were packed three deep along the edge of the makeshift dance floor, the whole middle of it moving as one animal under the purple bulbs Jaemin screwed into the fixtures. Someone spilled something sticky near the coffee table, but everyone was far too drunk to be concerned about such a minor thing. The air was hot in a way that had nothing to do with heating, it was a hundred and some people breathing in a house built for forty. The reeking scent of alcohol, sweat, and burnt sugar of the punch bowl threaded through her nostrils with marijuana from somewhere upstairs. It was, truly, an experience she could never forget.

The bass came up through her heels, sitting in her sternum. As if that wasn't bad enough, her wings got caught on someone's elbow, one strap sliding. She'd reached back to fix it without breaking stride.

And the dark haired boy kept pace beside her without appearing to try at all, which was the infuriating part. She was moving fast, cutting angles between people, chin up, eyes forward, tracking the cat ears bobbing determinedly ten feet ahead. Haechan was doing absolutely none of that, he was simply walking the way he walked down a hallway on a Tuesday, cup held low against his thigh, other hand back in his pocket, and people came apart in front of him without question.

"No response, pretty?" he coos from behind her, leaning over her shoulder.

"Nope," she practically yelled over the bass, not turning around.

"Hm."

She stepped around a boy dressed as a hot dog. "You should go back," she hums, voice entirely pleasant, "your friend might wonder where you went."

The two stop around a corner, finally, only because she was growing tired of having to push through the bodies.

"My friend," he repeats, amusedly, raising a brow in puzzlement.

"Yerim."

"Right," he nods, tipping his head back to take a drink of whatever substance he had in his cup.

She narrowed her eyes at him in blatant annoyance, before she spun around and started on her path again. A group of girls came through the gap ahead of them in a chain, hands linked, the one at the front navigating and the three behind shrieking with their eyes closed. Haechan stopped walking for exactly as long as it took them to pass, then started again. Solar had to take two quick steps to get level with him, which only irritated her more.

"Sure were eager to give her your number," she monotones once he was close enough to hear her.

He took another sip of his drink, eyes peering into it to find it emptier than he'd hoped, "could you tell?"

She didn't answer that, she knew it was just another poor attempt to get under her skin. "Why?"

"She asked."

"Everyone asks you shit constantly."

"Mm," he agrees, finishing his drink that time, "correct, and I quite enjoy saying no."

"So—"

"—You introduced us," he states, as if it was obvious.

She opened her mouth, then closed it again, not knowing the proper words to say to that. Someone behind them screamed, "SHOTS\!" at a volume that made a girl near the wall flench, dropping a slice of pizza face down on the hardwood, and Solar Lee was standing there like an idiot without a single thing to say.

He seemed to find this deeply satisfying, looking out over the top of the crowd toward the kitchen doorway, chin up, scanning, like the conversation had reached it's natural conclusion on schedule.

It was taking everything in her to fight her urges, absolutely everything.

She didn't want to seem desperate, or like a complete idiot, like she was obsessed. She was not, and she would stand on such a fact.

"You going to answer her?" she blurts out anyway, "She's going to text you, she's thrilled, you know."

His head came around about fifteen degrees, "Oh, you think?"

"You know what," she breathes, "nothing."

She turned away again, feeling the heat of her cheeks taking over her face.

"Ask me again," he intones, "I liked the way it sounded."

Her head whips to glare at him, reaching over and shoving him in the shoulder, hard enough to move him half a step sideways into a girl in a bedsheet, who didn't notice. "Do not say that again," she curses, "I will kill you."

"Sure, princess," he recovered the step without looking down, a smirk playing on his lips.

"Be quiet\!"

"Relax," he coaxes, "no one's listening to us, you're the only person in this room who thinks anyone's paying attention."

He was right.

Two feet away, a boy was explaining something to another boy by holding both of his shoulders. Someone had started a chant, then the song changed, the room making a noise like a wave breaking. Forty people put their hands up at once, and the two of them stood inside all of it like a pocket of still air.

They came around the back of a knot of people, the crowd thinning out for a stretch of about four feet, a little clearing where a speaker cable ran across the floor and everyone had learned to walk around it. And in that space, he looked sideways at her, properly.

But his eyes did not land on her face.

The choker was ridiculous. It was black, elastic, a little tight, pulled out the back of the bathroom cabinet at ten to eight because Hanni had used half a tube of concealer with color corrector yet still hadn't been able to cover it entirely. Solar felt his eyes land on it the way she'd have felt a finger.

Her hand flew up before she could stop it, two fingers hooking under the band at the side of her neck. "Don't," she warns firmly.

"I didn't say anything."

"You don't need to," she huffs, "I can see where you're looking."

"Just interesting," he shrugs, "you're the one wearing a choker, little out of place, no?"

"Yeah, thanks to you\!" she hisses, stepping over the cable.

He didn't answer that one, he crushed the empty cup in one hand instead as they passed the end of the sofa, chunking it into a bin bag someone had taped to the banister. Solar didn't look back, she couldn't, she just stared straight ahead, ears gone hot. She could feel it, and she knew from experience that they went red before anything else did.

I hate him, she decided, walking beside him through his own house with a hundred people screaming around them. I hate that I like it, and that's arguably ten times worse.

Up ahead, Yerim had located Hyein and Hanni against the far wall by the good window that didn't stick, where the air came in. She was already reporting to them, boasting, speaking with both of her hands in dramatic gestures, one hand still holding her phone. Just as she was nearing them, Haechan leaned over her shoulder to whisper, "don't forget your drink, pretty."

"Why don't you—" she finally turns to him, starting, but he was already gone through the crowd of bodies. Irritated and in utter disbelief from what just happened, she huffs into the toxic smell of a college party, grumbling under her breath, "fucking jerk, seriously."

She couldn't admit to the fact she was going to keep falling for it.

"So, he says, nobody has it," Yerim had been yelling at the two girls over the booming bass of the speakers, squeaking in excitement.

"Haechan said that?" Hyein confusedly confirms, her cup pressed against her collarbone with both hands, red extensions stuck to the side of her neck where she'd started to sweat.

"Yes, that's word for word what he said\!" Yerim nods eagerly.

The two girls exchange a look of genuine shock, before Hanni shrugs, "that sounds like something he would say, I suppose."

She was standing with her back to the window frame, one shoulder against it, holding her own cup at chest height, turning it slowly by the rim without drinking any of it. Her voice was working very hard to be a completely normal voice.

At the sight of Solar walking up, Hyein had stood up fully to push her cup into the girls hand without looking at her, eyes still focused on Yerim so that she didn't get suspicious. It was a poor attempt to not only distract her, but before Solar could even ask, Yerim continued, "he took my phone out of my hand, you guys, I thought I was going to fall on my face right in front of him," she notices the new presence then, looking to Solar with beaming irises, "right, Solar, did you notice, was I embarrassing?\!"

"Uh," Solar clears her throat, not having expected to be thrown into the conversation like that, "no, you did great."

Her tone was flatter than usual, but Yerim was too happy to notice. "Thank God," she exhaled, "I was so worried I was like, too forward."

Solar made a noise of understanding, before Hyein had taken over the conversation again to allow her some time to process, which she was thankful for. So, she'd ripped her eyes away and drank from the cup she'd been handed, which was warm and sweet, in a way that coated the roof of her mouth, and it had come out of a bowl Jeno had been touching. Behind Yerim's shoulder, a boy in half a Roman soldier costume was trying to get up onto the arm of the sofa and being pulled back down by two of his friends, patiently, like a routine they'd performed several times already. Hanni reached over to grab her forearm for moral support.

"I shouldn't text him, right?" Yerim was saying, nervously, "Yeah, that would be terrible, I'm not gonna text him."

"Yeah, definitely don't," Hyein agrees quickly.

"I'll sit with it," she declares, "for like... three days."

"Three days sounds good," the girl continues to make small talk about it, with the gravity of a woman signing a treaty. She peeled an extension off her neck and flipped it back over her shoulder, "it's a strategy, you know, make him wait."

"You're so right\!"

"Make him ache," she adds, with dramatics, causing Hanni, who was angled behind her, to kick her shin as a way to tell her to relax a little.

"Totally what I was thinking," Yerim was gushing, pressing both hands flat against her cheeks, phone and all, the way people do when they're trying to physically hold their face still. "God, he's so much nicer than people say he is," she shares thoughtfully, looking up towards the ceiling in a daydream, "I should've talked to him sooner."

Solar heard the sentence coming from a long ways away and couldn't seem to run fast enough. The irony burned through her veins enough to hurt, and she had to tilt her head back to force another gulp of the drink down her throat.

"Yeah," Hyein was muttering, seeming to lose some of her pizzazz from the fact she was glancing back at her friend, realizing she was likely about to lose her mind, "yeah, you could — you could say that."

"He's not so bad\!" Hanni cheerily cuts in to save it.

Realizing her cup was now empty, Solar sets it down on the ledge, her impulses beginning to take over her.

"He's not though."

Her two friend's heads whip to peer at her with concerned expressions. Hanni's grip tightens on her arm, but Solar had pushed her hand off and crossed her them over her chest. "I'm not trying to be rude, I just don't want you to get hurt," she shrugs, "he's not always like that."

She framed it as care, like a girl that was trying to be helpful, who knew the boys of Sigma Chi better than the one she was talking to. Although she'd almost slipped, she recovered because it was something she was good at. That was the environment she was raised in, being good at always saying the right thing, knowing how to say something without using the words directly, getting someone to believe exactly what you want them to. All of those things weren't inherently something to be proud of, and they were things she didn't want to use.

But she was her father's daughter.

"That's really good to know, actually," Yerim sighed, her face rearranging into gratitude, "you guys are so helpful, I can't thank you enough, Solar."

"Of course," Solar smiles, "I'm happy to help."

Yerim was grinning like a happy child, and turned to Hyein again to talk about something else. Hanni had taken that chance to lean over, "Sol—"

"—Don't," she cuts her off immediately, presuming she was going to say something she didn't want to hear.

"I was going to ask if you wanted—"

"—No, I'm fine, Han," she shakes her head, taking a deep breath, before noticing a weird bitter taste in her mouth, grimacing, "Jesus, what the fuck did Jeno put in that punch?"

"Nothing good," a voice cut in that was not any of the three girls, and her head whips up to see him. He came through the crowd the way he moved through every room in the house, which was to say that people got out of his way while he didn't notice them doing so. A girl in a leotard and rabbit ears said something to him as he passed, to which he didn't even turn his head.

Haechan had a fresh cup in his left hand, and something else in his right. The horns were still crooked in his hair, one of them knocked further off centre now. Solar had reached the point where she couldn't seem to look away from them, biting down on her lip and looking back down at her feet.

Yerim had beamed at the sight of him there, likely guessing that he was there because of her. He was going to let her think that, too, which was the gruel of it all. He'd greeted her and made small talk for a moment before he turned towards Solar again, raising a brow in question, "you didn't actually drink it, did you?"

Her eyes were narrowed as they met his, unimpressed, "it wasn't that bad, it was just a bit—"

"—Strong," he finishes her sentence for her, "yeah, that's what happens when you dump an entire bottle of whiskey in a punch bowl." He didn't let her say anything to that, because he'd held out whatever he'd been holding in his right hand, catching her entirely off guard.

Slowly, she looks down at his hand, which was holding a can, out of all things. It was cold enough that the outside had gone wet, slick, shining pink and black under the purple bulbs, beading at the rim. He'd opened it somewhere between the kitchen and there, walking, one handed.

"Take it," he urges.

She purses her lips in a straight line, snatching the can out of his fingers. There was no other move available to her in front of four people, and the cold of it went straight up through her palm, into her wrist. She didn't know why she had been so worried, since Yerim wasn't even paying attention, until she'd turned around to suddenly see Solar holding a Monster.

"Hold on," she cries, "where'd you even get that?"

"The fridge," Haechan responds for her, flatly.

"You guys have Monster?" Yerim pends, confused but intrigued at this new information, "Since when?\! I looked in there last week and there was like nothing in it\!"

The boy just shrugs, "Guess you didn't look properly."

And that was the whole of it, it was the entire explanation he'd provide, delivered to a point somewhere past Yerim's ear. The girl stared down at the can for another half second with the mild, unsuspicious puzzlement of a person who's noticed an inconsistency in a story she has no reason whatsoever to read closely, before Hyein made a small strangled noise beside her and Yerim turned to see what was wrong with her. The entire thing deflated and disappeared somewhere into the distant past.

Her brain told her to open her mouth and say something. Really, she could say thank you, say something simple that seemed harmlessly friendly and entirely casual. For someone innocent, like Yerim, it would read as absolutely nothing.

The words would not come out of her mouth. And next to her, she watched Yerim continue to converse, telling a story about one of her recent group projects that had gone horribly wrong, looking at Haechan every few seconds to see if he was still listening. The girl was so blatantly thrilled at the fact the Sigma boy she had a crush on, for longer than Solar even knew, was finally giving her an ounce of attention, all because a girl who had a class with him and was constantly seen hanging around those certain boys introduced them.

The worst part of it all was that there was no bad intent in her eyes. Yerim's eyes were bright and full of life, she was not someone who looked at a person and thought about a bad thing, she was a person who smiled and told someone they should keep their head up after noticing they seemed down.

And Solar watched her gleaming and giggling out some stupid story and couldn't find it in herself to think anything ill of the fact she was simply happy about a boy listening to her story.

So, she stood there, and drank her Monster, listening along to the story and smiling when everyone else did. She didn't let herself look at Haechan again for another five minutes.

"Solar Lee, Hanni Pham, Hyein Lee," a booming voice called from the side, and Jaemin entered their proximity with his arms in the air. He smelled horridly of smoke that coaxed them in it's stench as he stopped, winking at the three girls, before he noticed the other two people, "Oh, and you must be Alpha too, correct?" His eyes landed on Haechan, and he blinked a few times, registering this fact, thinking back to a morning in a kitchen and feeling a few things click in his brain. "Making the rounds, Haechannie?" He said it in a slightly teasing, playful tone.

Haechan was not impressed. "Do not call me that," he deadpans, "literally ever again."

"God," Jaemin waves a hand in the air, "you need to take a dab, dude."

"Nice to meet you, by the way\!" Yerim chimed, noticing that it was now her chance to speak, "Yes, I am Alpha, and I have been attending your parties for quite some time — well, since we've been permitted to, that is."

Jaemin stared down at the girl for a few seconds, "Fabulous, I am ecstatic you were... permitted," he says the word slowly, clearly confused about such a thing. Alpha Phi was indeed weird. "As always, ladies, please enjoy," he bows gently, eyes red as a demon from how high he was, "oh, and I am deeply looking forward to the thirteenth."

"Us too\!" Hyein screamed as he was walking away.

"Oh, yeah," Yerim cried, turning back to Haechan, "speaking of, are you looking forward to the joint trip, Haechan?"

From the second she opened her mouth, he seemed to already know what she was going to ask. The boy focused on taking another drink, before he'd exhaled, "Mm, I don't know if I'd say that."

"Why not?" the girl puzzles, "It seems so nice to me, four days in nature."

"Yeah," Hyein agrees instantly, "what's wrong with a camping trip?"

"It's fucking cold," Solar interrupts, "for one."

"Oh, come on," Hyein groans, "girl, you've lived here you're entire life."

"Okay, that doesn't mean I want to go camping in negative degree weather\!"

Haechan had yet to speak because of the abrupt banter. Yerim was too entertained to even remember she had asked him, snickering away as she watched the two girls. And he, he was fixated on watching a frustrated Solar Lee complain about a camping trip she supposedly dreaded and was horrified of while noticing the way the corners of her eyes crinkled at the ends.

By the time Hyein kept arguing with Solar, just to annoy her by that point, Solar had given an entire speech on how ridiculous the fact they were going camping in November was, especially because of the fact they'd only be closer to the lakes, meaning it would only be colder.

When she finished, none of them said anything for a minute.

"You've got a point," Haechan states first.

Solar tried not to look at him, she was afraid her eyes would give it away if she did.

"You really do," Yerim was pondering, "I wonder why they decided to go camping in November."

None of them had the answer, because there wasn't a complex answer to be had, not at least for something as minuscule as that.

The conversation continued peacefully, to her surprise. Hanni kept grabbing Solar's forearm and squeezing every few minutes, letting her know she was still present, telling her telepathically it was going to be okay. Hyein, if she noticed anything was off, would instantly become the center of attention again, which Solar appreciated in a way she would never be able to put into words.

And she did entirely fine.

It's okay, she thought then, I'm not bothered, I can do this and be totally okay.

\-

Mark arrived at twenty past nine.

The first thing anyone noticed about him was the fact he'd wore his costume again, properly, and clearly had taken it very seriously. The glasses were back, tie hanging loose, white button down, his hair combed and gelled. Everyone else in the house was wearing the corpse of last Friday, but he'd politely ironed his.

He didn't do a straight walk towards the group. Instead, he makes his rounds, as Jaemin would put it, letting the room engulf him, stopping by crowds to say hello, bro hugging some guys he knew from his classes, making jokes with other fraternity members Solar had never met. It wasn't that it wasn't clear where he was going, but he was taking his time doing it, because Mark Lee was a guy that people liked, he was simple, easy, and he knew how to be presentable in a completely harmless way.

But, when his eyes found Solar Lee, the room could feel the shift, even over the booming music. The change in his face was instant and genuine, a smile breaking across his lips with enough warmth that something uncomfortable turned over in her stomach. He raised two fingers in a wave, beginning to push through the bodies separating them after bidding who he was talking to farewell.

Solar watched his eyes make the trip in order as he approached, from Hanni, to Hyein, to Yerim's cat ears, and then to Haechan standing less than three feet away, red crooked horns in his dark hair. His lips formed a thin line, eyes carefully lingering on the can in her hands.

It could be nothing, really. It was just an energy drink, not a declaration of love, he tried to tell himself. He wasn't dumb, he knew Haechan was going to keep pursuing Solar no matter what, it was who he was. And even worse, he knew nothing he said was going to change Solar's mind, not unless he made it good enough.

"Well, look who it is," Hyein cried, "Superman makes his appearance\!" She threw both of her arms in the air in a cheer, being the loud, bright girl everyone adored her as.

"Clark Kent," Mark corrects as he finally stops by the group, pushing the glasses up his nose with one knuckle, "there's a difference, you know," he adds, before nodding his head towards Yerim, warmly, "hey, by the way, I'm Mark."

Yerim was gleaming, evidently having a hard time holding her excitement back from what was happening in front of her. She had never had much interaction with any of the Sigma boys, not since whatever happened last year that everyone was so secretive about. "Hi, I'm Yerim\!" she chirps, shaking his hand that he held out with both of hers, "I know who you are, obviously, everyone does."

Mark chuckled, "Well, that's kind of ominous."

"Well like, in a good way\!" Yerim assures him cheerily.

Though, that wasn't entirely true. There were people who didn't remember Mark Lee in the most positive light, but most of the campus had buried the story to the back of their minds.

No one who wasn't on campus last year would ever know, because people didn't talk about it, not anymore. Therefore, it was the easiest thing for Mark Lee to arrive at a group of five people and make everyone of them feel like the one he'd come over for. He did it without calculating it, which Solar had spent two weeks trying to decide whether she believed. But tonight, watching him do it to a girl he'd met five seconds ago, she believed it.

He greeted Hanni, said something to Hyein about the extensions that made her flip them over her shoulder like a woman in an advertisement. Then, he'd nodded at Haechan, an ordinary nod, the kind you give someone you've known since you were twelve and are currently not in a fight with, and Haechan returned about sixty percent of it. Neither of them made it apparent, nor a thing, because there were four girls standing there and both of them were, in their own ways, extremely skilled at rooms.

And while the girls continued to chat, Yerim pulling Haechan into the conversation every waking opportunity she got, Mark turned his attention to Solar. The gold at the corner of her eyes, orange satin, wings that had already come loose once, all of it seemed to register in pieces before his smile softened into something smaller.

"Stella returns," he voices jokingly, "that's — that's her name, right?"

"Yes," Solar giggles, "yes, that's her name, though I'm prefer if you use mine," she pauses suddenly, realizing the way that sounded, before clearing her throat, "like, my name."

Mark nodded, chuckling from her stuttering, eyes nervously glancing down to his feet. "Well, Sol, you look better the second time," he hums, "if that was even possible."

It was sweet, that was the aggravating part of him, how gracefully he could make something sweet without appearing to know he was doing it. Solar felt herself smile before she could decide if she wanted to, and beside her, Hanni made a tiny noise into her cup, having overheard the conversation.

"Thanks, Mark."

Haechan didn't move from where he was, nodding along as if he was listening to whatever the girls were talking about. He stood with one shoulder turned partially toward the wall, fresh drink hanging loose in his hand, other still buried inside the pocket of his black jeans. His expression was bored enough to be convincing to anyone who'd never watched him become still on purpose.

It was Mark who finally turned towards his old friend, eyes scanning him, before he pipes, "nice costume, Hyuck."

Haechan tipped his head until one of the red horns caught the orange light, "put a lot of thought into it," he deadpans, "though, not as much as you, clearly."

"That's obvious."

"Oh," Yerim interrupted, innocently, remembering the most fascinating development of her evening, "did you know you guys keep Monster in the fridge? I literally looked last week and didn't even see it\!"

The tension was sharp enough to suffocate.

Hanni stopped turning her cup, Hyein's lips folded inward so abruptly that half of her mouth disappeared. And Solar, who'd spent her entire life learning how to remain pleasant while people had a charged, passive aggressive exchange that was secretly, entirely about her, smiled like nothing was happening and took another drink.

Mark's gaze dropped to the can again. He lived here, he knew what occupied the fridge better than any of them did, it was typically beer, expired condiments, and whatever meal Renjun had bought three days earlier and written his name across in permanent marker.

"Huh," he breathes, "no, I didn't know we had any either."

"We're blind, Mark," Yerim shrugs, "Haechan must have laser vision or something."

The bass moved through the floor.

And Haechan, unbothered, took another drink of his cup before humming, "you could say that."

Suddenly, the can felt like it was freezing the blood in her hand, up her arm. Mark nodded once, slowly, before the smile returned to his face, and he laughed, lightly, "yeah, guess I need to check the fridge more often."

"That's unlike you, Marky, you're usually great at checking things regularly," Haechan monotones, tapping a finger against his cup casually, as if he was in thought. There were stickers in his word, poking out and daring him to bite. Yerim, of course, didn't have the slightest clue what was going on. To her, it sounded like two best friends bantering. Although she'd heard the rumors about them fighting, she and most students didn't take them seriously. These were two boys who had been inseparable since they came on campus, after all.

Hyein and Hanni, on the other hand, looked like they were seconds from passing out. Hyein was clearly trying to keep her mouth shut, and to help with that, Hanni was gripping her hand with her own as a warning that it would only make the situation much worse.

But at the sight of Mark opening his mouth to speak, the girl decided that someone had to do something, and Solar looked like she was lost in a trance. So, Hyein steps forward, letting go of Hanni's hand to clap her hands together, "okay\!" The clap was with enough force that Yerim jumped from surprise. She steps in between the two boys, before anyone could find another harmless sentence to load with something terrible. "Anyone wanna dance? I didn't spend six hours fixing these costumes so everyone could stand against a wall and look constipated\!"

"I don't think that's what constipation looks like, Hyein," Yerim had puzzled in confusion at her sudden interruption, since everything seemed normal to her.

"It's a metaphor, Yerim\!" Hyein snaps sassily, annoyed she didn't understand.

"Not exactly," Hanni mumbled, gently.

Nonetheless, her distraction worked for now, as the conversation dissolved before it could become anything else. Yerim burst into giggles, Hanni reached out to fit the top of one of her cat ears, and someone behind them knocked into the window hard enough that they all had to take a collective step forward.

Mark ended up beside Solar from the movement, shoulder brushing the edge of one of her wings. "Sorry," he offers, carefully reaching behind her to straighten it rather than letting the strap remain twisted, "these are for real a public safety hazard."

Solar snorts, "Hey, I didn't make them."

"Don't you dare," Hyein overhears with a gasp, in the midst of grabbing Yerim's hand to lead her towards the dance floor, "the craftsmanship is flawless, which means you are the problem\!"

Then, she was gone into the crowds of bodies with Yerim, who was screeching like a child. Hanni lingered behind, a nervous look on her face as she slowly watched the three. When she caught Solar's eyes, she mouthed, are you going to be okay?

Since she was still standing in front of the two, she smiles and offers a single nod in the girl's direction. Despite how unsure she looked, she exhales, giving her a thumbs up before turning and heading to the outskirts of the crowd. She was going to stay in the area, so she could be there for back up if needed, but another girl from Alpha caught her and dragged her away into another conversation.

"I was looking for you," Mark shares once it was just the three of them, angling himself so he wasn't even able to see Haechan, who had moved back to his original spot, leaning against the wall feet away, close enough to still hear, "I got stuck across campus, then Jeno told me I had to stay upstairs unless I put on my costume."

Solar laughs then, knowing that he was genuinely being serious which only made it funnier. "Yeah, well, rules are rules," she returns.

"I know," he groans, "sucks I have to follow them, you know, being a man of the people and all."

"Man of the people?" she raises a brow, physically wincing, "What, were you solving crime on campus?"

"Of course, and it takes a lot out of me," he defends, holding a hand to his chest, "saving the city plus maintaining a demanding social calendar."

"Mark, your parties happen in your living room."

"Exactly, no commute though\!"

Her laugh came out before she could stop it again, and Mark beamed from earning it, leaning in slightly so he could hear over the music. Haechan stayed where he was throughout the entire conversation, close enough that his silence acquired weight, drinking from his cup like he had nowhere better to be.

A couple of girls noticed him there, seemingly alone, and came over to try their luck. Solar tried not to glance over as he began blankly talking to him, how he tended to talk to most people.

"You're gonna hate me for asking," Mark had knocked her back out of her thoughts, "but — did you happen to save another dance for me?"

She snapped her eyes back onto his. "Oh my God, no, you were way too bad last time," she shakes her head, teasingly.

"Aw, come on," he complains, "I wasn't that bad."

Solar rolled her eyes, trying to think of what she could say next. It wasn't that she didn't want to dance with him, she just knew what people would think if she did. And as far as she knew, Danielle was lingering around there somewhere.

Still, she was too engrossed in talking to Mark then to notice the presence of Chenle, who materialized at Haechan's shoulder with his hands buried in the pocket of a grey hoodie, wearing the profoundly inconvenienced expression of someone who'd been forced to leave his room on a Friday night. He took in the environment, Solar and Mark feet away, two girls in rather scandalous costumes orbiting him with desperation, and the cup in his hands that was nearly empty.

"Come outside," he mutters, leaning over Haechan's shoulder so he could hear.

Haechan didn't turn or even acknowledge him, he just kept listening to whatever the girls were spouting, "no."

"Dude, come on," Chenle huffs, "Jaemin ordered food and sent it to the wrong gate."

"Sounds like a personal problem to me, Chenle."

"Yeah, it became a personal problem when he obnoxiously thought it appropriate to give the driver my number," he grumbles, glancing down as his phone buzzed inside his pocket, "now I'm making it yours."

Haechan sighs, "take Jisung."

Chenle stared at him for a second, eyes moving down to the drink again. "That's your fifth, man," he states quietly.

His jaw shifted in response, the smallest movement, and the boredom in his face sharpened into annoyance. "You're irritating," he exhales, offering a nod towards the two girls as he pushes himself off the wall.

He didn't say anything to her nor Mark, but his eyes caught hers before he followed Chenle towards the kitchen.

Something settled in her stomach, her mind racing as she wondered what was going on. Chenle was good, her brain told her, Chenle wouldn't enable things like that.

"Alright," she chimes, locking back onto Mark and forcing a grin on her face, "fine, let's dance."

\-

The delivery driver had gone to the back entrance of the neighboring building, which Chenle found impressive considering Jaemin's instructions contained the words large white fraternity house with a bunch of drunk people outside.

By the time they found him, the man was standing beside his car with six pizza boxes stacked to his chin and the specific look of someone reconsidering every choice that had led him there. Haechan took four of the boxes without greeting him, while Chenle took the other two, thanked him, and began walking back towards the house.

They took the side gate since it was closer, padding through the green grass across the ginormous yard. There were indeed drunk people outside, even in the cold weather. It seemed that when a college student had enough alcohol, they no longer cared how cold it was because they couldn't feel it by that point.

Looping around the back where it was quieter, Haechan was heading for the door. But Chenle had stopped beside the brick of the house, where the music became duller and less violent, placing his two boxes on the concrete.

The dark haired boy made it three steps before he realized.

"What are you doing?" he deadpans, turning to look down at the boy who'd casually sat on the concrete against the brick of the house.

"Eating."

"Inside exists," he monotones, "you hate being outside."

"This is true," he confirms, flipping open the top box. Steam rolled into the November air, carrying cheese and grease with it. The boy says nothing else to that, he just pulls out a slice and holds it out to him.

"I'm not hungry."

"You haven't ate anything, so that's a lie."

"You don't know that."

"You've had five drinks in the last thirty minutes," he informs, still holding the pizza between them, "and have not ate anything since you had four earlier."

Haechan's face didn't change, though something in his eyes flickered, "you counting everyone tonight?"

"No," he shrugs, "most idiots announce it themselves."

From inside the house, the song changed and a hundred bodies answered it at once, the sound pushing through the windows before the walls swallowed it again. Haechan looked toward the windows without actually looking at anything in particular, the pizza boxes balanced against his forearms.

"You're not clever," he sighs finally, "this isn't how it works."

"Just eat," was his blank response, because he already knew that. A slice of pizza wasn't going to cure the problem, anyone would know that.

Haechan shakes his head in disbelief, shifting the stack into one arm before snatching the slice from him with the other, taking an irritated bite large enough to end the conversation. Chenle nodded, as if a hypothesis had been confirmed, reaching into the plastic delivery bag for one of the water bottles Jaemin ordered.

He chunked one at Haechan without saying anything.

And the two boys sat there and ate pizza without saying anything else. He didn't ask about Solar, Mark, not about the cup Haechan had emptied before following him or the fact his drinking had accelerated the second Mark walked in the room. The blonde boy simply ate his own slice beside the brick wall, watching the delivery driver make a three point turn at the end of the street.

That was the arrangement he offered, whether Haechan understood it or not. Food, cold air, and a number accurate enough that it couldn't be argued with.

After a few minutes, Haechan finished the slice, opening a water. Taking three long drinks, he twists the cap back on, balancing the bottle on top of the boxes against his arm.

"You done?"

Chenle looked down at the four pizza boxes left beside him, "clearly not."

Haechan rolled his eyes before spinning on his heel, "I'm going inside."

The boy had rose to his feet with his own boxes moments later to follow him, figuring he had done enough.

And he had, because Haechan didn't reach for another cup when they went inside.

Back inside, Solar managed to forget about the certain dark haired boy for forty minutes, which wasn't really her fault. Hyein had somehow convinced whoever was doctoring the music to play her favorite song at the moment, which was HOT TO GO, and had began to jump around screaming with her arms in the air. Olivia arrived in the middle of it, and at the sight of Hyein screaming, she started screaming and jumping herself. And before she knew it, Solar and Hanni had been pulled into the mix, while a giggly, smiling Mark watched the entire encounter.

Jeno's shift at the door had ended, meaning he'd traded the responsibility of judging other people's costumes for standing on a coffee table pushed to the side of the dance floor. As if that alone wasn't bad enough, he'd begun attempting to pour shots into people's mouths, who excitedly surrounded him like he was some kind of saint.

One of those people happened to be Jisung, who had tilted his head back, only to get vodka poured into his eye.

"Bro\!" he cried, stumbling backward with both hands over his face, "what the fuck is wrong with you?\!"

"You moved\!" Jeno defended, nearly falling off the table as he pointed at him in exasperation, "why would you move, dumb ass?\!"

"Because you were pouring it into my fucking eye\!"

"Okay, well that's not where I was aiming\!"

"That just makes it worse\!"

The entire circle dissolved into laughter, including Solar, who had stopped dancing with her friends to witness the scene happening on the sidelines. She started giggling so hard she had to grab onto Mark's shoulder to keep herself upright, watching as Jisung grumpily snatched the bottle out of Jeno's hand to take a drink of it himself.

It was easy with him. Mark danced without taking himself seriously, badly enough that she could make fun of him, yet well enough that she kept dancing anyway. His hand had stayed at her waist without wandering, warm and familiar against the orange satin. Whenever the crowd shoved them closer, he'd laugh and apologize as if he'd personally invented gravity.

There were parts of him she trusted without thinking, which was what made the rest so difficult.

Somewhere near the window, after Hyein and the friends had gone to take a break from the chaos, Jaemin had cornered Hyein and was holding the edge of one of her wings between two fingers, studying the stitching with more seriousness than he'd displayed during any chapter meeting.

"So, how much would I owe you?"

Hyein blinked at him, since it was the first thing he'd said to her. "Huh?"

"For a commission," he clarifies, pulling his phone out with eyes so red he could barely focus on the screen, "I need something for December, like festive — but not ugly festive, I refuse to look like a department store."

The girl's eyes widened with delight, and she stood up a bit straighter as if she was presenting herself. "You're for real?\!"

"Duh," he deadpans, "I'm always serious about being hot, Hyein, this should be a known fact between us."

She laughed in half amusement and half disbelief, "well, I require a deposit, and you're not getting a friend discount because you called my wings a hazard last week," she states matter of factly, seeming to find her confidence amidst the surprise.

"Businesswoman," Jaemin hums, pleased, "I respect it, my lady."

Hanni appeared beside them, having been looking for where her friend wandered off to. At the sight of Jaemin, she grinned, offering a greeting. Hyein didn't waste any time to fill her in on what just happened.

"Oh, Jaemin," she chimes just as the conversation about commissions was wrapping up, "did you remember to finish you guys' side of the camping transport assignment?"

He'd practically lit up at the question, focusing back on the two girls and beginning to explain to them everything he had planned for the trip, which was much more than a simple assignment. The conversation quickly turned into costumes, cabin numbers, and a spreadsheet he was desperately trying to convince Hanni he'd looked at, when it was painfully obvious he had not.

Solar saw Haechan return with Chenle through the back door out of the corner of her eye, carrying two pizza boxes through the kitchen doorway. He'd taken the horns off at some point, and they were now hanging around the neck of the half empty water bottle balanced atop the four pizza boxes he was holding.

He looked entirely normal, which was the least reassuring thing about him.

Chenle said something to him that he answered without looking, setting the pizzas onto the counter while a crowd immediately pounced on the food. He left the water bottle beside the boxes, but didn't spare any of the alcohol a glance.

Though, before she could begin to think about the meaning behind that, Mark had spun her underneath his arm with such little warning one of her wings hit him in the face. She'd seemingly forgotten what they were even doing by that point.

"Ow," he chuckled, catching it before it bent, "see? Total hazard."

"That was your fault," she accuses, gently slapping his chest.

"Maybe, still a hazard," he insists, grinning down at her. She found herself smiling back, because she was having fun. It didn't have to be anymore complicated than that, did it? There was no crime in enjoying a person who continued to be kind to her, even with her suspicions, no betrayal in laughing when they were funny. Haechan had given another girl his number less than an hour ago, and perhaps more importantly, had never asked her not to dance with Mark.

There was a lot she didn't know, and a lot of questions she wished she had answers to.

But she was going to enjoy herself until she got them, at the very least.

She felt his eyes from across the room anyway.

The sensation arrived first at the back of her neck, where the choker sat slightly too tight. Solar glanced toward the kitchen before she could talk herself out of it, finding him leaning against the end of the island through the doorway, empty hands resting against the granite behind him. Another girl she didn't recognize was leaning over the counter trying to make conversation with him, but his eyes didn't leave hers, not even despite the people moving in front of him every few seconds.

Then he'd tipped his head somewhere towards the back hallway, a small enough motion that no one else would ever think was meant for them.

She ripped her eyes away first, waiting through the rest of the song.

"Mark," she calls over the music, as the next one was already starting, "I'm going to the bathroom," she informs him, "and before you ask, no, I don't need you to keep watch, and yes, I'm going to the one down here."

His eyes studied hers carefully, searching. Something flashed through his expression, before he'd sent her a small smile, nodding, "okay, yeah, I'll be here."

She knew he wanted to ask more, that he was already thinking of the inevitable. Still, he watched her go, before turning away towards Jisung, who was still trying to flush whiskey out of his eye on the side of the room with a bottle of water rather than in a sink, for some reason. Solar cut towards the opposite direction, around the end of the stairs and into the narrow back hallway between the pantry and laundry room.

Naturally, he was already there, leaning beside the closed laundry room door with his arms crossed, horns hanging loosely from two fingers. The music was quieter there but no absent, bass traveling through the pipes, making the framed evacuation map on the wall tremble.

"Four minutes," she states, stopping in front of him with her arms crossed over her chest.

"Only four?" he hums, eyes moving down her body and back up with little attempt at subtlety.

"You wasted most of it giving..." she cut herself off, closing her eyes and taking a deep breath. Instead, she turned away and put her hands on her upper arms, rubbing them up and down to create warmth, "it's cold back here," she mutters bitterly.

"It's November," he returns, "it's going to be cold most places."

"Thank you, Donghyuck, I hadn't gotten to that conclusion yet," she snaps sarcastically.

Something dark flashed in those irises from the sound of that name, but he didn't move a muscle. "You're annoyed," he observes, "worried about your sorority sister?"

He didn't have to finish his question for her to know what he was referring to. Solar glares at him, clearly irritated and unable to hide it. "Shut up, I didn't even say anything about that," she hisses, "sounds to me like you wanted me to mention it."

"Sweetheart, don't think I don't know what you were really going to say."

"Fuck off," she huffs, "I don't care if my sorority sister wants to text you."

"You're the one who introduced us."

"Okay?\!" she cries, "I said I don't care," she turns away from him again, not wanting him to be able to read her face, "either way, you could've said no."

"Mm, you could've, too."

"You are so..." she starts again, then stops herself, "whatever, Haechan, is this what you wanted? I'm kind of on a time limit here."

"Oh, Marky's got you tied down that much, huh?"

"You'd like to know, wouldn't you?\!" she snapped, louder than she meant for it to be.

His lips formed a straight line the second the words entered his ears, like they'd slapped him across the face.

Silence takes over them for a few minutes, and his eyes wander away towards the ceiling in a brief moment of thought. She wondered if it was enough, if he was finally going to tell her something about any of this, even if it was small.

"Just don't let him get you alone, princess."

The sentence was so abrupt she wasn't sure if she'd heard it correctly, "seriously?" Her body stiffened before she had time to decide how angry that made her. It was the command of it, the way both of them seemed to believe they could point at the other and expect her to arrange her life around a warning they refused to explain.

"You don't get to tell me that," she asserts stubbornly, pointing an accusatory finger at his chest.

Haechan's jaw shifted, but he didn't answer by making himself crueler, "I know."

The correction took some of the force out of the argument before she could use it, only making her more annoyed. "Do you?"

"Mm," he nods, glancing once toward the mouth of the hallway where Mark was likely lingering, "I'm just telling you what he's waiting for."

"No, you're not telling me anything," she exclaims, "that's the entire problem, Haechan\!"

For once, he actually looked stressed, closing his eyes for a second and pinching the bridge of his nose. "He's waiting for a room without witnesses," he finally deadpans, seeming to find the correct words.

The bass rattled through the wall. Solar couldn't help but stare at him, searching his face for the rest and finding that he'd already decided how much he'd give her. "To do what?\!"

His gaze dropped to the floor for half a second before meeting her eyes again, "you don't have to listen, princess."

"That doesn't — okay, you know what? Fine," she groans, "you're fucking unbelievable."

"So I'm told."

She looked back up at him then, the way his fringe fell into his eyes, and the only thing she could seem to think was that he's scared.

It arrived fully formed, fitting perfectly, because she'd built it herself twenty four hours ago in an empty lecture hall. Jealousy, her brain told her, he's dressing it up as a warning because he can't say the other thing out loud.

She wanted to believe it, a part of her did believe it. But the smarter part knew there was so much more than that. She'd have to be an idiot not to, with all of the rumors and whispers flying around, with all of the odd comments from Danielle.

He knows, he knows something about a girl, about Mark, and about himself, and Jaehyun knows it too.

But how was she ever going to find out?
